senses.title: Run to meet: the Latin core sense
senses.titleCN: 迎面跑去：拉丁语的本义
senses.definition: in the original Latin sense, to run toward something and meet it, including meeting an opponent in argument
senses.definitionCN: 按拉丁语本义，跑向某物并与之相遇，也包括在争论中迎上对手
senses.example: Latin occurrere described two people or things running toward each other until they met.
senses.exampleCN: 拉丁语 occurrere 描述两方在奔跑中相互靠近，直到碰上。
senses.why: Latin occurrere joined ob 'against, toward' to currere 'to run'. The first picture is a head-on meeting, not an accident and not a thought.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 occurrere 把 ob“迎着、朝着”与 currere“跑”组合起来。最初的画面是迎面相遇，既不是事故，也不是念头。

senses.title: Happen: take place
senses.definition: to happen, especially without being planned or looked for
senses.definitionCN: 发生，尤指并非计划之中或特意寻找的
senses.example: The accident occurred at the crossroads just after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 事故就发生在午夜过后的十字路口。
senses.why: From 'meet' the word moved to 'present itself in the course of events'. An event that meets you on the road is an event that happens to you.
senses.whyCN: 从“相遇”出发，这个词转向“在事件进程中自己浮现”。在路上迎上你的事，就是发生在你身上的事。

senses.title: Happen at a stated time or place
senses.definition: to take place at a particular point in time or in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 在特定的时间点或特定地点发生
senses.example: The festival occurs in the first week of June.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日在六月的第一周举行。
senses.why: Once an event is pictured as meeting you, it can be pinned to a spot on the road and a moment on the clock.
senses.whyCN: 一旦事件被想象成与你相遇，它就能被钉在路上的某个地点和时钟上的某个时刻。

senses.title: Be found to exist: occur in nature
senses.titleCN: 存在于某处：自然界里有它
senses.definition: to be found or to exist in a place, a group, or a natural setting
senses.definitionCN: 在某地、某群体或自然环境中被发现、存在
senses.example: This orchid occurs only in the high wetlands of the north.
senses.exampleCN: 这种兰花只生长在北部的髙地湿地。
senses.why: If a thing presents itself when you go looking, it 'occurs' there: the meeting becomes a record of where it can be met.
senses.whyCN: 如果去找就能遇见，它就是“occur”在那里：相遇变成了“何处能遇见它”的记录。

senses.title: Appear in a text or a list
senses.definition: to appear in a piece of writing, a list, or a set of data
senses.definitionCN: 出现在文章、名单或一组数据中
senses.example: The word 'harbour' occurs four times in the first paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: harbour 这个词在第一段出现了四次。
senses.why: A page is a road too: the reader runs along it, and every word that meets the eye 'occurs' at that point.
senses.whyCN: 书页也是一条路：读者沿着它跑，每一个撞进眼睛的词就在那一点“occur”。

senses.title: Come into the mind: occur to someone
senses.definition: in the pattern occur to someone, of an idea: to come into a person's mind
senses.definitionCN: 用于 occur to someone 结构，指想法进入某人脑中
senses.example: It never occurred to me to check the date on the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 我从没想到要去核对信上的日期。
senses.why: The 1620s added the mental branch: a thought runs toward you and meets you, seemingly from outside, which is why English says the idea occurred rather than 'I thought it'.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 20 年代增加了心理分支：一个念头朝你跑来并遇上你，好像来自外部，所以英语说“想法 occur 了”，而不是“我想到了它”。

senses.title: Exist in a particular form or variety
senses.definition: to exist in a particular form, type, or variety, often one of several
senses.definitionCN: 以某种形态、类型或变体存在，常是若干种之一
senses.example: The mineral occurs in two distinct crystal forms.
senses.exampleCN: 这种矿物以两种不同的晶体形态存在。
senses.why: The 'be met with' sense narrows to how a thing is met: the form it presents when you encounter it.
senses.whyCN: “能被遇见”的义项收窄为“以何种样子被遇见”：你碰到它时它呈现的形态。

senses.title: Occur to someone to do: an idea that prompts action
senses.titleCN: 想到要去做：推动行动的念头
senses.definition: in the pattern it occurs to someone to do something, of an idea that suggests an action
senses.definitionCN: 用于 「it occurs to someone to do something」 结构，指想到该做某事
senses.example: It occurred to her to call the police before leaving.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开前想到该报警。
senses.why: The mental meeting can carry a plan as well as a fact: what meets the mind is not only 'that something is so' but 'that something should be done'.
senses.whyCN: 心理上的相遇既能带来事实，也能带来计划：撞进脑子的不只是“事情如此”，还有“应该去做”。

intro.en: Occur entered English in the 1520s meaning 'meet, meet in argument', from Latin occurrere 'run to meet'. The sense 'happen' and the mental sense 'come into the mind' followed within a century.
intro.cn: occur 于 16 世纪 20 年代进入英语，意为“相遇、在争论中迎上”，来自拉丁语 occurrere“跑去相遇”。“发生”义与“想到”义在一个世纪内相继出现。

items.en: First recorded meaning 'meet, meet in argument', with the physical head-on meeting still visible in the word.
items.cn: 最早记录为“相遇、在争论中迎上”，词里仍看得见那种物理性的迎面相遇。

items.en: From French occurrer 'happen unexpectedly', or directly from Latin occurrere.
items.cn: 来自法语 occurrer“意外发生”，或直接来自拉丁语 occurrere。

items.en: Latin occurrere 'run to meet, run against, befall, present itself' is ob 'against, toward' plus currere 'to run'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 occurrere“跑去相遇、迎面撞上、降临、自己出现”由 ob“迎着、朝向”加 currere“跑”构成。

items.en: Currere goes back to PIE *kers- 'to run', the root also seen in current and excursion.
items.cn: currere 追溯到原始印欧语 *kers-“跑”，current 与 excursion 也出自这个词根。

items.en: The noun occurrence is recorded from the 1530s; the sense 'come into one's mind' appears in the 1620s.
items.cn: 名词 occurrence 自 16 世纪 30 年代有记录；“想到”义出现于 17 世纪 20 年代。

items.en: Modern English keeps the event sense as the main one and leaves the literal meeting to the root; occurrence, co-occur and recur carry the family forward.
items.cn: 现代英语以事件义为主，把字面的“相遇”留在词根里；occurrence、co-occur、recur 延续了这个词族。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to fill space, time or attention. It shares oc-/ob- and the -py ending shape but comes from capere 'to grasp', not currere 'to run'.
entries.definitionCN: 占据空间、时间或注意力。它形似 occur，但词根是 capere“抓”，不是 currere“跑”。

entries.definition: an event, or the fact of something happening. It is the noun from occur, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 事件；发生。它是 occur 派生的名词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: to happen again. It uses re- 'again' plus the same currere 'to run' root.
entries.definitionCN: 再次发生。它用 re-“再次”加同一个 currere“跑”词根。

entries.definition: to take place, usually by chance. It is the plain everyday word, while occur is more formal and often written.
entries.definitionCN: 发生，通常带偶然意味。它是最平实的日常词，occur 更正式，多用于书面。

entries.definition: to happen or become known. It is formal and often suggests that facts emerged gradually.
entries.definitionCN: 发生；逐渐为人所知。它偏正式，常暗示事实慢慢显露。

entries.definition: to come into being, especially of problems or situations. It points to a source, while occur only records that something took place.
entries.definitionCN: 产生，尤指问题或局面。它指向来源，occur 只记录某事发生了。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin ob plus currere, the currere family in current and excursion, and the fixed pattern occur to someone.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁成分 ob + currere，current 与 excursion 中的 currere 词族，以及固定结构 occur to someone。

normal.en: ob 'toward' plus currere 'to run' gives 'run to meet': something comes at you and you meet it.
normal.cn: ob“朝向”加 currere“跑”就是“跑去相遇”：有东西朝你而来，你与它撞上。

normal.en: Current, excursion, concur and recur all share currere 'to run', the root that makes occur a meeting.
normal.cn: current、excursion、concur、recur 都含 currere“跑”，正是这个词根让 occur 成为一次相遇。

normal.en: Obtain uses tenere 'to hold' and occupy uses capere 'to grasp': the same ob- prefix, three different roots.
normal.cn: obtain 用 tenere“握持”，occupy 用 capere“抓”：同一个 ob- 前缀，三个不同词根。

normal.en: It never occurred to me is the mental branch: the idea runs up to you from outside.
normal.cn: it never occurred to me 是心理分支：念头从外面跑到你面前。

normal.en: Occurrence, co-occur and recur are the everyday nouns and verbs built on the same stem.
normal.cn: occurrence、co-occur、recur 是由同一词干构成的日常名词和动词。

abstract.en: Picture two runners on one road, each heading straight for the other: that collision is the original occur.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条路上两个奔跑的人，各自直冲对方：那次相撞就是 occur 的原型。

abstract.en: An event can run at you the same way, which is why a fault or an accident 'occurs' rather than simply being there.
abstract.cn: 事件也能以同样的方式朝你跑来，所以故障或事故是“occur”，而不只是“在那里”。

abstract.en: A thought can run at you too: it appears from outside, meets the mind, and is reported as occurred.
abstract.cn: 念头也会朝你跑来：它从外面出现，撞上你的心，被说成“occur 了”。

examples.en: Most errors in the survey occurred where the form was printed in two columns.
examples.cn: 问卷中的大多数错误发生在表格排成两栏的地方。

examples.en: It occurred to him only later that the key had been left in the door.
examples.cn: 他后来才想到钥匙被留在了门上。

examples.en: These fish occur in every river along the coast.
examples.cn: 这种鱼在沿海每条河里都有分布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，扣儿」——哦，扣儿！扣子突然掉了，事情就这样发生了 → occur 发生、出现

root: 源自拉丁语 occurrere“跑去相遇、迎面撞上”= ob-“迎着、朝向”+ currere“跑”（PIE *kers-“跑”），核心是“朝你跑来并撞见”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of occur all start from one picture: something runs toward you on the same road. The meeting then becomes an event, a location, a line in a text, a form in nature, and finally an idea that arrives in the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: occur 的八个义项都从同一幅画出发：有东西在同一条路上朝你跑来。那次相遇随后变成事件、地点、文本里的一行、自然界中的一种形态，最后变成抵达脑中的念头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something running toward you on the same road until it meets you.
core.cn: 核心意象：有东西在同一条路上朝你跑来，直到与你相遇。

branches.en: THE LITERAL MEETING: the Latin head-on encounter, including meeting an opponent in argument.
branches.cn: 字面的相遇：拉丁语里的迎面撞见，也包括争论中迎上对手。

branches.en: THE EVENT: what presents itself in the course of things, and can be pinned to a time and place.
branches.cn: 事件：在事情进程中自己出现的东西，可以被钉在某个时间与地点。

branches.en: THE FOUND THING: where a species or mineral can be met, and in what form it presents itself.
branches.cn: 被遇见之物：物种或矿物能在何处遇到，以及它以什么形态出现。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN PAGE: the road becomes a text, and each word meets the reader at a point.
branches.cn: 书页：路变成文本，每个词在某个位置与读者相遇。

branches.en: THE MIND: an idea runs up to you, either as a fact noticed or as an action suggested.
branches.cn: 心念：念头跑到你面前，或者作为一个被注意到的事实，或者作为一件该做的事。

intro.en: Occur is Latin ob- 'toward, against' plus currere 'to run', with the verb ending -ere. English keeps the stem occurr- and adds -ence, -ent and the prefixes co- and re-.
intro.cn: occur 由拉丁语 ob-“迎着、朝向”加 currere“跑”和动词词尾 -ere 构成。英语保留词干 occurr-，并加 -ence、-ent 以及前缀 co-、re-。

latinIntro.en: The direct source is Latin occurrere, from ob and currere; currere 'to run' is the root shared by current, course and excursion.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是拉丁语 occurrere，由 ob 与 currere 构成；currere“跑”是 current、course、excursion 共有的词根。

items.meaning: to run to meet; to present itself, happen, or come to mind
items.meaningCN: 迎面相遇；出现；发生；想到
items.example: The same problem occurs in every third sample.
items.exampleCN: 每三个样本中就有一个出现同样的问题。

items.meaning: the fact of happening, or an event that happens
items.meaningCN: 发生；发生的事件（-ence 构成名词）
items.example: Power cuts are a weekly occurrence here.

items.meaning: happening at a particular time; incidental
items.meaningCN: 正在发生的；偶然发生的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: The occurrent noise came from the lift shaft.
items.exampleCN: 当时那阵声响来自电梯井。

items.meaning: to happen or appear at the same time
items.meaningCN: 同时发生；共现（co- 表“共同”）
items.example: Rain and strong wind often co-occur in this valley.
items.exampleCN: 在这个山谷里，降雨和大风常常同时出现。

items.meaning: to run back again, hence to happen once more
items.meaningCN: 再次发生；复发（re-“再次”+ currere“跑”）
items.exampleCN: 疼痛每年春天都会复发。

items.example: Doctors watch for a recurrence of the tumour.
items.exampleCN: 医生密切留意肿瘤是否复发。

items.meaning: running or flowing now; a flow of water or power
items.example: The current carries the boat downstream.

items.meaning: a running out, hence a short journey
items.meaningCN: 远足；短途旅行（ex-“出”+ currere“跑”）
items.example: The class took a one-day excursion to the coast.
items.exampleCN: 全班去海边做了一日短途旅行。

items.meaning: to run together, hence to agree or happen at once
items.meaningCN: 同时发生；同意（con-“共同”+ currere“跑”）
items.example: Both experts concur with the report's conclusion.
items.exampleCN: 两位专家都同意报告的结论。

items.meaning: to run into something, hence to bring upon oneself
items.meaningCN: 招致；蒙受（in-“进入”+ currere“跑”，即“撞上”）
items.example: Late payment will incur a fine.

latinEntries.meaning: to run to meet, run against, befall, present itself
latinEntries.meaningCN: 跑去相遇；迎面撞上；降临；自己出现

definition_zh: 海洋；大洋；一片汪洋；大量
definition_en: the vast body of salt water that surrounds the continents and covers most of the earth
core_image: 一整片连成一体的咸水把陆地围在中间，望不到对岸，也数不清有多少层浪
scene: 地理课上，老师转动地球仪，指着连成一片的蓝色说，A single ocean can hold more water than all the land it surrounds.
sceneCN: 这里 ocean 指「地球上环绕陆地的巨大咸水体」（第 1 个义项：连成整体、覆盖大部分地表的咸水）；句意为：一个海洋能容纳的水量超过它周围全部陆地；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 海洋；大洋；（喻）大量、无边无际的一片
远洋的；海运的（如远洋货运、远洋航行）

derivatives.zh: 海洋的；辽阔如海的
海洋学
海洋学家
大型海洋水族馆
海滨地段；临海的
海洋研究；海洋学（较旧的说法）

senses.title: The world-encircling body of salt water
senses.titleCN: 覆盖地球大部分表面的连片咸水
senses.definition: the great body of salt water that surrounds the continents and covers most of the planet
senses.definitionCN: 环绕各大陆、覆盖地球大部分表面的巨大咸水体
senses.example: A single ocean can hold more water than all the land it surrounds.
senses.exampleCN: 一个海洋能容纳的水量超过它周围全部陆地。
senses.why: Greek Okeanos named the stream believed to run all the way around the world, so the word began as one continuous encircling water, not as a list of separate seas.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 Okeanos 原本指绕世界一周的大河，所以这个词从诞生起就是「一圈连着的咸水」，而非若干彼此分开的海。

senses.title: One of the named divisions
senses.titleCN: 五大洋中一个有名字的洋
senses.definition: one of the five large divisions of this water, such as the Pacific, Atlantic or Indian ocean
senses.definitionCN: 这片水域被划分出的五大洋之一，如太平洋、大西洋或印度洋
senses.example: The Atlantic ocean narrows toward its northern end.
senses.exampleCN: 大西洋在它的北端变窄。
senses.why: once geographers divided the single world water into named basins, the same word served both the whole and each part, and context decides which is meant.
senses.whyCN: 地理学家把这一整片世界水域划分成有名字的海盆之后，同一个词既指整体也指其中一部分，靠上下文决定所指。

senses.title: The water as opposed to the land
senses.definition: the open salt water thought of as a place distinct from land, especially in travel and trade
senses.definitionCN: 与陆地相对的开阔咸水，尤用于航行与贸易语境
senses.example: They spent three weeks on the ocean before sighting land.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海上待了三个星期才看见陆地。
senses.why: a voyage needs two settings, land and water; the word supplies the second one, so 'on the ocean' simply means out on the salt water.
senses.whyCN: 一次远航需要两个场景：陆地与水面；这个词提供后者，因此「在海洋上」就是身处开阔咸水之中。

senses.title: A very large amount
senses.definition: an immense quantity of something, especially something abstract such as words or work
senses.definitionCN: 某事物数量极大，尤指话语、工作等抽象事物
senses.example: An ocean of paperwork awaited the new clerk.
senses.exampleCN: 海量的文书工作等着这位新职员。
senses.why: the figurative step is simple: the largest thing most speakers know becomes the measure of anything too big to count, so an ocean of forms is just too many forms.
senses.whyCN: 比喻的跳跃很简单：把说话人知道的最大之物拿来度量多到数不清的东西，因此「一整个海洋的表格」就是表格多到数不清。

senses.title: A boundless expanse
senses.definition: a vast unbroken stretch of something that seems to have no edge, such as sand or grass
senses.definitionCN: 沙、草等铺展到看不见边界的广阔一片
senses.example: An ocean of sand stretched from the road to the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 一片沙海从路边一直铺到地平线。
senses.why: the eye reads any surface without a visible edge the way it reads water, so desert and prairie borrow the word for the same feeling of no boundary.
senses.whyCN: 人眼看到没有可见边界的表面时，读法与看水面一样，因此沙漠与草原借这个词表达同样的「无边」之感。

senses.title: A depth of feeling
senses.definition: an overwhelming quantity of a feeling that seems to swallow a person up
senses.definitionCN: 铺天盖地、仿佛把人吞没的情感
senses.example: She sank into an ocean of grief after the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼之后，她沉入一片悲痛的汪洋。
senses.why: deep water is the standing image for what cannot be crossed or controlled, so grief and doubt are described as oceans, with the person inside them rather than beside them.
senses.whyCN: 深水一直是无从跨越、无法掌控的意象，因此悲伤与疑虑被说成海洋，而人是在其中，不在其旁。

senses.title: The ocean as a climate system
senses.definition: the salt water regarded as a system that stores heat, moves currents and regulates the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 把咸水视为储存热量、驱动洋流并调节大气的一个系统
senses.example: The ocean absorbs much of the heat trapped by greenhouse gases.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋吸收了温室气体截留的大部分热量。
senses.why: twentieth-century earth science turned the place into a mechanism: the same water that sails are built for is now studied as a store and pump of heat.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的地球科学把这个地点变成了机制：原本造船航行的同一片水，如今被当作热量的储库与泵来研究。

senses.title: The high seas in law
senses.definition: open water beyond any state's coastal jurisdiction, belonging to no single country
senses.definitionCN: 超出任何国家沿海管辖范围、不属任何一国所有的开阔水域
senses.example: Beyond the twelve-mile limit lies the open ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 越过十二海里界限，就是开阔的公海。
senses.why: maritime law needed a term for water that no flag claims; the everyday word for the great water took that legal slot without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 海商法需要一个词指没有任何国旗主张的水域，于是日常指大水的词原样填进了这个法律位置。

senses.title: Ocean as a shipping modifier
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean carried by, used on, or belonging to the open sea
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示由远洋承运、用于远洋或属于远洋的
senses.example: Ocean freight moves most goods between continents.
senses.exampleCN: 远洋货运承担了洲际间的大部分货物。
senses.why: when a noun is placed before another noun it stops naming a place and starts naming a route or a class, which is how ocean becomes the label on a shipping container.
senses.whyCN: 名词放到另一个名词前时，它不再指地点，而开始指一条路线或一个类别，海洋就是这样变成了集装箱上的运输标签。

intro.en: Ocean reaches English through Latin and Old French from Greek Okeanos, the name of the stream that was thought to run around the whole inhabited world. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ocean 经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，源头是希腊语 Okeanos——古人想象中环绕整个已知世界的大河之名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Okeanos in Homer is the river that encircles the disc of the world and is never crossed; it is a proper name first, a common noun for the outer water later.
items.cn: 荷马笔下的 Okeanos 是环绕世界圆盘、无人能越的大河；它先是专名，后来才成为指外围水域的普通名词。

items.en: Later Greek writers, above all Herodotus, used okeanos for the open water outside the Mediterranean, and the word began to mean the sea itself rather than a river.
items.cn: 后来的希腊作者，尤其是希罗多德，用 okeanos 指地中海之外的开阔水域，这个词开始表示海本身而非一条河。

items.en: Latin took Oceanus as both a name and a common noun for the great sea; the adjective oceanicus 'of the ocean' follows the same stem.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 Oceanus 同时用作专名与指大海洋的普通名词；形容词 oceanicus「海洋的」沿用同一词干。

items.en: Old French occean passed the word to Middle English around the fourteenth century, where it first named the outer sea and only later any large body of salt water.
items.cn: 古法语 occean 在 14 世纪前后把这个词传给中古英语，最初指外围的大海，后来才泛指任何巨大咸水体。

items.en: From the age of exploration the single world water was mapped as named oceans, and the older 'stream around the world' image survives only in poetry and etymology.
items.cn: 从大航海时代起，这一整片世界水域被绘制成有名字的几个大洋，古老「绕世大河」的意象只留在诗歌与词源说明里。

items.en: Source uncertain (root origin, not first date): the deeper origin of Greek Okeanos is disputed, with some scholars treating it as a pre-Greek loan; any reconstructed Indo-European form for it is a hypothesis, not an established derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（指词根来源，不是首见年代）：希腊语 Okeanos 的更早来源有争议，有学者视之为前希腊语借词；为它构拟的任何印欧语形式都只是假说，不是已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like ocean or are built on the same stem; group two holds words for water that differ in size or register.
note.cn: 第一组是与 ocean 形近或同出同一词干的词；第二组是都指水域、但规模或语体不同的词。

entries.definition: the collective name for the Pacific islands and Australia; it adds -ia to the Oceanus stem, so it names a region, not a body of water.
entries.definitionCN: 太平洋岛屿与澳大利亚的合称；在 Oceanus 词干上加 -ia，指一个区域，而不是一片水域。

entries.definition: ocean plus -ic: relating to the ocean, or simply very large and open, as in oceanic distances.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 -ic：与海洋有关的，或形容极其辽阔开阔的，如「远洋般的距离」。

entries.definition: ocean plus -graphy 'writing, describing': the scientific study of the sea, not the sea itself.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 -graphy「书写、描述」：对海洋的科学研究，而不是海洋本身。

entries.definition: ocean plus front: land that faces the sea, so the compound names property rather than water.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 front：面朝大海的陆地，因此这个复合词指地产，而非水域。

entries.definition: a body of salt water smaller than an ocean and often partly enclosed by land; the everyday word for the water you can see from a shore.
entries.definitionCN: 比大洋小、常被陆地部分围住的咸水体；指岸边看得见的那片水的日常用词。

entries.definition: a plural used for a particular stretch of water, as in territorial waters; it is neutral in size and common in law and news.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，指某一片特定水域，如领海；不限定规模，常见于法律与新闻。

entries.definition: an old poetic word for the open sea, as in the Spanish Main; it survives mostly in verse and historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 指开阔大海的古雅诗歌用词，如「西班牙海」；如今多存于诗歌与历史写作。

entries.definition: the deep is a literary name for the sea that stresses its depth rather than its width; it fits images of sinking and hiding.
entries.definitionCN: the deep 是海洋的文学称呼，强调深度而非广度；适合「沉没、隐藏」一类意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek Okeanos was the river around the world, so the word began as one continuous ring of water.
normal.cn: 希腊语 Okeanos 是绕世界的大河，因此这个词最初就是一圈连着的水。

normal.en: The family runs ocean, oceanic, oceanography, oceanographer, oceanarium, oceanfront.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ocean、oceanic、oceanography、oceanographer、oceanarium、oceanfront。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical sense: ocean floor, ocean basin, deep ocean, open ocean.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理义：海底、海盆、深海、开阔洋面。

normal.en: Geography names five: the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic oceans.
normal.cn: 地理学列出五个：太平洋、大西洋、印度洋、南大洋与北冰洋。

normal.en: The idiom an ocean of means a huge amount, as in an ocean of paperwork.
normal.cn: 短语 an ocean of 表示极多，如海量文书。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of water that cannot find a shore to belong to.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴水找不到可以归属的岸。

abstract.en: Picture a map where the blue is not a colour but a distance you cannot cross.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，上面的蓝色不是颜色，而是一段跨不过去的距离。

abstract.en: Picture a voice heard across water, arriving in layers like waves.
abstract.cn: 想象隔着水传来的人声，一层一层像浪一样抵达。

examples.en: The ocean covers about seventy percent of the earth's surface.
examples.cn: 海洋覆盖了地球表面约七成。

examples.en: Scientists track how the ocean moves heat from the tropics poleward.
examples.cn: 科学家追踪海洋如何把热量从热带向极地输送。

examples.en: From the cliff we watched an ocean of cloud roll inland.
examples.cn: 从崖上望去，我们看着一片云海向内陆翻滚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，深海」——看到望不到边的水，先「哦」一声，再想到深海大洋 → 海洋、大量

root: 希腊 Okeanos「环绕世界的大河」（专名转普通名词）→ 拉丁 Oceanus → 古法语 occean → 英语 ocean；Okeanos 的更早来源有争议，或为前希腊语借词，构拟的印欧形式均属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses radiate from one picture: a ring of salt water around the land, then the named parts, the water seen from a ship, the same boundlessness borrowed for quantity and feeling, and finally the water studied as a machine and claimed in law.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从同一个画面辐射出去：环绕陆地的咸水圈，然后是其中命名分区、船上所见的水面，同一份「无边」被借去指数量与情感，最后是当作机器研究的海洋与法律主张的海域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one continuous ring of salt water holding the land inside it, too wide to see across.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整圈连着的咸水把陆地围在里面，宽到看不见对岸。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BODY: the same water is first a place on the map and later a heat store studied by climate science.
branches.cn: 物理水体：同一片水先是地图上的一个地点，后来成为气候科学研究的储热系统。

branches.en: DIVIDED AND CLAIMED: geography cuts the whole into named oceans, and law marks where national claims stop.
branches.cn: 被划分与被主张：地理学把整体切成有名字的洋，法律标出国家主张止于何处。

branches.en: SEEN FROM A SHIP: from deck the water is a setting for travel, and as a modifier it labels the freight that crosses it.
branches.cn: 从船上看见：在甲板上水是旅行的场景，作定语时则标注穿越它的货运。

branches.en: BORROWED SCALE: the widest thing a speaker knows measures paperwork, sand and grass.
branches.cn: 借来的尺度：说话人知道的最宽之物，被用来度量文书、沙与草。

branches.en: INWARD WATER: grief and doubt become oceans because the person is inside them, not beside them.
branches.cn: 向内的水：悲伤与疑虑变成海洋，因为人是在其中，而不是在其旁。

intro.en: Ocean is a borrowed proper name that became a common noun; its family is built with Greek and Latin suffixes added to the same stem.
intro.cn: ocean 是一个转为普通名词的外来专名；它的词族都是在同一词干上加希腊语与拉丁语后缀构成的。

latinIntro.en: Latin Oceanus keeps both the name and the common noun, and oceanicus supplies the adjective pattern behind oceanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 Oceanus 同时保留专名与普通名词用法，oceanicus 则提供了 oceanic 背后的形容词构词模式。

items.meaningCN: 古人想象中环绕世界的大河

items.example: Oceanography combines chemistry, physics and biology.

items.meaning: a large enclosure for living sea animals

items.meaning: the island region of the Pacific

latinEntries.meaningCN: 外围的大海；亦为海神之名

scene: 深夜的实验室里，一个人对着满屏的浮标轨迹标出一股暖流的路径。The oceanographer traced the warm current from a year of buoy data.

senses.title: A scientist of the sea
senses.definition: a scientist whose work is the study of the ocean as a physical, chemical, biological and geological system
senses.definitionCN: 以研究海洋的物理、化学、生物与地质系统为工作的科学家
senses.example: The oceanographer traced the warm current from a year of buoy data.
senses.exampleCN: 这位海洋学家凭一年的浮标数据追出了那股暖流的路径。
senses.why: Oceanographer is the Greek compound for sea description with -graphos 'one who writes', so the word means 'one who writes down the sea'.
senses.whyCN: oceanographer 是希腊语中「描述海洋」的复合词加上 -graphos「书写者」，因此这个词意为「把海洋写下来的人」。

senses.title: A physical oceanographer
senses.definition: one who studies currents, waves, mixing and the transport of heat and salt
senses.definitionCN: 研究海流、波浪、混合与热盐输运的人
senses.example: The physical oceanographer modelled the overflow across the sill.
senses.exampleCN: 这位物理海洋学家模拟了越过海槛的溢流。
senses.why: Physics supplies the equations for motion, so its practitioners take the main name with a branch adjective.
senses.whyCN: 物理学提供运动的方程，其从业者便在主名之前加一个分支形容词。

senses.title: A chemical oceanographer
senses.definition: one who studies dissolved gases, nutrients and the chemistry of seawater
senses.definitionCN: 研究溶解气体、营养盐与海水化学的人
senses.example: The chemical oceanographer measured the oxygen minimum layer.
senses.exampleCN: 这位化学海洋学家测了最小含氧层。
senses.why: Seawater is a solution, so a chemist can spend a career on what is dissolved in it.
senses.whyCN: 海水是一种溶液，化学家可以终身研究其中溶解的东西。

senses.title: A geological oceanographer
senses.definition: one who studies the sea floor, its sediments and the history they record
senses.definitionCN: 研究海底、其沉积物及所记历史的人
senses.example: The geological oceanographer dated the ash layer in the core.
senses.exampleCN: 这位地质海洋学家测定了岩芯中火山灰层的年代。
senses.why: The floor preserves a sequence, so a geologist reads the sea as a stratified archive.
senses.whyCN: 海底保存着层序，因此地质学家把海当作分层的档案来读。

senses.title: A biological oceanographer
senses.definition: one who studies marine organisms and their relation to the water they live in
senses.definitionCN: 研究海洋生物及其与所处水体关系的人
senses.example: The biological oceanographer counted the copepods from each tow.
senses.exampleCN: 这位生物海洋学家数了每一网拖上来的桡足类。
senses.why: Life in the sea cannot be separated from the water, so the biological worker keeps the oceanographic name.
senses.whyCN: 海中的生命无法与海水分开，因此生物工作者也保留海洋学的名号。

senses.title: A member of a research cruise
senses.definition: a scientist who sails on a research vessel to collect data at stations
senses.definitionCN: 随科考船出海、在各站位采集数据的科学家
senses.example: The oceanographer stood watch from midnight until four.
senses.exampleCN: 这位海洋学家从午夜值班到四点。
senses.why: Fieldwork defines the job as much as theory, and the person on watch is still called by the same name.
senses.whyCN: 野外工作与理论一样界定这份职业，值班的人仍用同一个称呼。

senses.title: An early surveying officer
senses.definition: in older usage, an officer or naturalist employed to sound and describe the sea
senses.definitionCN: 旧时受雇测深并描述海洋的军官或博物学者
senses.example: The oceanographer of the old survey filled four volumes with soundings.
senses.exampleCN: 那次旧调查的海洋调查员用四卷书记满了测深数据。
senses.why: Before specialised degrees, the -graphos sense was literal: the work was to write down what the lead line found.
senses.whyCN: 在专门学位出现之前，-graphos 的字面义仍在：工作就是把测锤探到的东西写下来。

senses.title: Anyone who sounds a vast unknown
senses.titleCN: 比喻：探究深不可测领域的人
senses.definition: a person who patiently investigates something vast and hard to see into
senses.definitionCN: 耐心探究某浩瀚而难以看清之物的人
senses.example: The oceanographer of the ministry's files knew where every report had sunk.
senses.exampleCN: 这位部委档案的「海洋学家」知道每份报告沉在哪里。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the person and the method: someone who lowers a line into a place others cannot see.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留人与方法：一个人把测线垂进他人看不见的地方。

intro.en: Oceanographer joins Greek okeanos 'ocean' with -graphos 'one who writes', the personal form of graphein. The word is a nineteenth-century coinage. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oceanographer 把希腊 okeanos「海洋」与 -graphos「书写者」组合起来，后者是 graphein 的人称形式。这个词是十九世纪的造词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Okeanos was the river encircling the world. Its origin is uncertain and probably pre-Greek.
items.cn: okeanos 是环绕世界的大河。其来源不确定，可能属前希腊语。

items.en: Graphein meant 'to write, draw, scratch', and its agent noun -graphos named a person who writes or draws.
items.cn: graphein 意为「书写、描画、刻划」，其施动名词 -graphos 指书写或描画的人。

items.en: Okeanos plus -graphos gave a word for one who describes the sea, built on the same pattern as geographer and cartographer.
items.cn: okeanos 加 -graphos 构成指「描述海洋的人」的词，与 geographer、cartographer 依同一范式。

items.en: As systematic expeditions began, the word moved from the writer of descriptions to the salaried scientific officer on a survey ship.
items.cn: 随着系统考察开始，这个词从「写描述的人」转为调查船上领薪的科学职员。

items.en: In the twentieth century the oceanographer became a trained specialist with a degree, a branch and a set of instruments.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，oceanographer 成了一位受过训练、有学位、有分支与一套仪器的专家。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): okeanos has no accepted Indo-European origin, so any form offered for it is a guess. The first date of the English word is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：okeanos 没有公认的印欧来源，为其提出的任何形式都是猜测。这个英语词的首见年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds the family forms of the same word; group two holds names for people who work on or with the sea.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词族中的各种形式；第二组是从事海洋工作或在海上工作者的名称。

entries.definition: The field of study; the -grapher form names the person who practises it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究领域；-grapher 形式指从事它的人。

entries.definition: Relating to the field or its work; it cannot name a person.
entries.definitionCN: 与领域或其工作有关；不能指人。

entries.definition: One who describes the earth's surface, built with the same -graphos; different object, same pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 描述地表的人，用同一个 -graphos 构成；对象不同，范式相同。

entries.definition: One who writes with light; the -graphos element survives with a very different medium.
entries.definitionCN: 以光书写的人；-graphos 这一成分在完全不同的媒介中留存。

entries.definition: A specialist in sea life; an oceanographer may study water, floor or circulation instead.
entries.definitionCN: 研究海洋生命的专家；海洋学家也可能研究水体、海底或环流。

entries.definition: One who measures and charts waters for navigation, a practical calling rather than a research career.
entries.definitionCN: 为航海测量并制图水域的人，属实务行业而非研究职业。

entries.definition: A scientist of the atmosphere; the two fields meet where sea and air exchange heat.
entries.definitionCN: 研究大气的科学家；两门学科在海气交换热量处相接。

entries.definition: A scientist of lakes and rivers, using similar tools on a different body of water.
entries.definitionCN: 研究湖泊与河流的科学家，用相似工具研究不同的水体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: -graphos is 'one who writes': an oceanographer is the person who writes down the sea.
normal.cn: -graphos 是「书写者」：oceanographer 就是把海洋写下来的人。

normal.en: The family runs ocean, oceanic, oceanography, oceanographic and oceanographer.
normal.cn: 同族词有 ocean、oceanic、oceanography、oceanographic 与 oceanographer。

normal.en: Branch adjectives name the speciality: physical, chemical, biological and geological oceanographer.
normal.cn: 分支形容词点出专长：物理、化学、生物与地质海洋学家。

normal.en: The pattern matches geographer and cartographer, both -grapher words.
normal.cn: 这个范式与 geographer、cartographer 相同，都是 -grapher 词。

normal.en: Watchkeeping is part of the job: the oceanographer stands a four-hour shift at sea.
normal.cn: 值班是工作的一部分：海洋学家在海上值四小时的班。

abstract.en: Picture someone holding a notebook on a deck while a wire disappears below.
abstract.cn: 想象有人站在甲板上拿着本子，钢缆在下方消失。

abstract.en: Picture a reader who keeps a lamp on a long pole to see the dark shelves.
abstract.cn: 想象一位读者用长杆上的灯去照黑暗的书架。

abstract.en: Picture a person who maps a country one sounding at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人一次一个测深点地绘出一个国家。

examples.en: The oceanographer spent three seasons on the same seamount.
examples.cn: 这位海洋学家在同一座海山上度过了三个季节。

examples.en: A chemical oceanographer joined the cruise to sample dissolved iron.
examples.cn: 一位化学海洋学家加入航次，采集溶解铁样品。

examples.en: The oceanographer's chart became the standard reference for the strait.
examples.cn: 这位海洋学家的海图成了该海峡的标准参考。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one person: the scientist of the sea, four branch specialists, the watchkeeper on a cruise, the early surveying officer, and finally anyone who lowers a line into a place others cannot see.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个人展开：研究海洋的科学家，四位分支专家，航次上的值班者，早期的调查官员，最后指任何把测线垂进他人看不见之处的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person on deck with a notebook while the wire goes down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人拿着本子站在甲板上，钢缆正向深处去。

branches.en: THE ROLE: -graphos fixes the person, and ocean fixes the object.
branches.cn: 角色：-graphos 定人，ocean 定对象。

branches.en: FOUR SPECIALITIES: water, chemistry, floor and life each produce a branch expert.
branches.cn: 四种专长：水体、化学、海底与生命各自产生一位分支专家。

branches.en: THE WATCH: the job is also a shift on deck, not only a degree.
branches.cn: 值班：这份职业也是甲板上的一班岗，而不只是一纸学位。

branches.en: EARLIER FORM: before degrees, the writing was literal and the title belonged to survey officers.
branches.cn: 较早形态：在学位之前，书写是字面的，名号属于调查官员。

branches.en: TRANSFERRED PERSON: anyone patient enough to sound a dark place inherits the figure.
branches.cn: 人物转移：任何有耐心探测黑暗之处的人都继承了这一形象。

intro.en: Oceanographer is a Greek-derived personal noun; the suffix -graphos is Greek, so no Latin entries are listed.
intro.cn: oceanographer 是希腊来源的人称名词，后缀 -graphos 属希腊语，因此不列拉丁词条。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved: okeanos and graphein are Greek, and the -graphos suffix reached English through Latin and French borrowings of Greek compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁词根：okeanos 与 graphein 是希腊语，-graphos 后缀是经拉丁语与法语借用希腊复合词而进入英语的。

senses.title: Not even: one left over after pairing
senses.titleCN: 奇数：两两配对后多出一个
senses.definition: of a number: having one left over when divided by two
senses.definitionCN: 指数目：被二除后余一
senses.example: Three is an odd number, so one chair is always empty.
senses.exampleCN: 三是奇数，所以总会空出一把椅子。
senses.why: Old Norse oddi meant 'a third or additional number', the unit beyond an even count. The oldest English sense is exactly this arithmetic one.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语 oddi 意为“第三个数、额外的数”，即成双之外多出的那一单位。英语最古老的义项正是这个算术义。

senses.title: Unpaired: the single one of a pair
senses.titleCN: 落单：一对里剩下的那只
senses.definition: of one of a pair: left without its partner and therefore unusable as a set
senses.definitionCN: 指一对中的一只：失去配对的另一只，因此无法成套使用
senses.example: One odd glove lay on the bench for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一只落单的手套在长椅上放了一周。
senses.why: The 'one over' count becomes a concrete object: if a pair is a set of two, the unit left over is the odd one, and the pair is broken.
senses.whyCN: “多出一个”的计数变成具体物件：一对是成双的集合，剩下的那一单位就是 odd，这一对也就散了。

senses.title: Occasional, not regular: odd jobs and odd moments
senses.titleCN: 零星的：不定时的零工与零碎时间
senses.definition: not forming part of a regular pattern; happening now and then
senses.definitionCN: 不构成规律的一部分；偶尔发生
senses.example: He takes odd jobs in the holidays to pay for books.
senses.exampleCN: 他假期打零工来买书。
senses.why: A job that does not belong to a regular set is the 'extra' unit again: isolated, unpaired, scattered through the week.
senses.whyCN: 不属于固定一套的活计又是那个“多余单位”：孤立、不成对、散落在一周里。

senses.title: Strange, peculiar
senses.definition: unusual or unexpected in a way that makes people uneasy or curious
senses.definitionCN: 不寻常或出乎意料，让人不安或好奇
senses.example: It was odd that the door stood unlocked all night.
senses.exampleCN: 门整夜没锁，这有点古怪。
senses.why: The 'strange' sense is recorded from the 1580s and grows from 'the odd one out': what does not fit the set draws attention and looks wrong.
senses.whyCN: “古怪”义自 16 世纪 80 年代有记录，从“落单的那一个”生长出来：不合群的东西招人注意，也显得不对劲。

senses.title: Slightly more than: forty-odd
senses.definition: used after a number to mean 'and a little more', as in forty-odd people
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字后表示“再多一点”，如 forty-odd people
senses.example: Thirty-odd people signed up for the night walk.
senses.exampleCN: 三十多个人报名参加了夜行。
senses.why: Here the leftover unit is attached to a round number: the count passes the round figure by an odd remainder, so the 'extra' becomes an approximation.
senses.whyCN: 这里多出的单位附在整数后面：数目超出整数一点点零头，于是“多余”变成约数。

senses.title: The odd one out: set apart from the group
senses.titleCN: 格格不入：被排除在群体之外
senses.definition: the person or thing that does not match the rest of a group
senses.definitionCN: 与群体其余成员不相配的人或物
senses.example: She was the odd one out in a family of musicians.
senses.exampleCN: 在一个音乐家家庭里，她是个例外。
senses.why: A set works by pairing; whoever cannot be paired is visibly separate. Being 'the odd one out' is the social version of the broken pair.
senses.whyCN: 一组东西靠配对成立；配不上对的那个就明显独立在外。“落单者”就是破碎配对的社会版本。

senses.title: Odds and ends: leftover scraps
senses.titleCN: 零碎杂物：用剩的边角料
senses.definition: in odds and ends, small useful items left over from larger things
senses.definitionCN: 用于 odds and ends，指大件用剩的小而有用之物
senses.example: The drawer was full of odds and ends: buttons, wire and old stamps.
senses.exampleCN: 抽屉里塞满零碎东西：纽扣、铁丝和旧邮票。
senses.why: The plural odds means unequal remainders; combined with ends, it names the scraps that no longer belong to any complete set.
senses.whyCN: 复数 odds 指不相等的余数；与 ends 连用，就命名了那些不再属于任何完整套组的边角料。

senses.title: Odds: the chances of an outcome
senses.titleCN: 赔率与可能性：成败的差距
senses.definition: in the plural noun odds, the probability of one result rather than another, used in betting and in general prediction
senses.definitionCN: 复数名词 odds 指某一结果相对另一结果的可能性，用于赌博与一般预测
senses.example: The odds are against a rookie winning this tournament.
senses.exampleCN: 新手赢得这次比赛的可能性不大。
senses.why: Odds began as unequal numbers, a ratio that is not even. Betting turned that imbalance into a measure of chance: the odds are the unevenness of outcomes.
senses.whyCN: odds 起初指不相等的数，即不成偶的比例。博彩把这种不平衡变成机会的量度：赔率就是结果之间的不均等。

senses.title: Odd Fellow: a member of a friendly society
senses.titleCN: Odd Fellow：互助会会员（历史用法）
senses.definition: in the name Odd Fellows, a member of a fraternal benefit society that grew from local clubs in the late 18th century and was formally organised in 1813
senses.definitionCN: 在 Odd Fellows 这一名称中，指兄弟互助会的成员；该会由 18 世纪末的地方社团发展而来，1813 年正式组织
senses.example: He joined the Odd Fellows in 1813 and paid a small weekly sum for sickness cover.
senses.exampleCN: 他于 1813 年加入 Odd Fellows，每周缴一小笔钱以备生病。
senses.why: The society's name uses odd in the older sense of 'unusual companions': members were fellows of an odd sort, set apart from ordinary clubs. Odd Fellows is recorded as a local society late in the 18th century.
senses.whyCN: 这个会名用的是 odd 较旧的“奇怪的伙伴”义：成员是些“古怪的同伴”，与普通社团不同。Odd Fellows 作为地方社团记录于 18 世纪晚期。

intro.en: Odd is recorded around 1300 from Old Norse oddi 'a third or additional number'. The Norse word literally meant 'point of land, angle', and the step from 'point' to 'third number' is a development special to that language, so it is best marked as generally accepted.
intro.cn: odd 约于 1300 年从古诺斯语 oddi“第三个数、额外的数”进入英语。这个诺斯语词字面是“尖角、土地的一角”，而从“尖点”到“第三个数”这一步是该语言特有的发展，故宜标为“一般认为”。

items.en: Odde is recorded meaning 'constituting a unit in excess of an even number', the arithmetic sense that English still keeps.
items.cn: odde 记录为“构成超出偶数的一个单位”，这是英语至今保留的算术义。

items.en: From Old Norse oddi 'third or additional number'. The same word also meant 'point of land, angle'.
items.cn: 来自古诺斯语 oddi“第三个数、额外的数”，同一个词还表示“土地的一角、尖角”。

items.en: Odda-maðr meant 'the third man, the one who breaks a tie', and odda-tala meant 'odd number', showing the 'extra unit' idea already at work.
items.cn: odda-maðr 指“第三个人、打破平票的人”，odda-tala 指“奇数”，说明“多余单位”的观念已在运作。

items.en: Oddi is related through oddr 'point of a weapon' to Proto-Germanic *uzdaz 'pointed upward', which also gives Old English ord 'spear point, beginning', German Ort 'place', and Lithuanian usnis 'thistle'. The link from 'point' to 'third number' is not found outside Norse and is source uncertain.
items.cn: oddi 经 oddr“武器尖端”与原始日耳曼语 *uzdaz“朝上的尖”相关，后者也给出古英语 ord“矛尖、起点”、德语 Ort“地点”和立陶宛语 usnis“蓟”。从“尖点”到“第三个数”这一步在诺斯语之外未见，来源不确定。

items.en: The sense 'strange, peculiar' is recorded from the 1580s, growing out of the idea of the one left out of the set; a favourable sense 'singular, remarkable' appears around 1400.
items.cn: “古怪、奇特”义自 16 世纪 80 年代有记录，由“被排除在套组之外的那一个”发展而来；约 1400 年已有“非凡、稀有”的褒义。

items.en: Modern English adds fixed phrases: odd job (1728), odd lot (1897), and the Odd Fellows society, a local club in the late 18th century and formally organised in 1813.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了固定说法：odd job（1728）、odd lot（1897），以及 Odd Fellows 互助会——18 世纪晚期为地方社团，1813 年正式组织。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: a poem addressed to a person or thing. It sounds the same as odd but comes from Greek oide 'song'.
entries.definitionCN: 献给某人或某物的颂诗。它与 odd 同音，但词源是希腊语 oide“歌”。

entries.definition: the plural of odd in its 'unequal remainder' sense: chances, or odds and ends. It is not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: odd 在“不相等余数”义上的复数：可能性、赔率或零碎杂物。它不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: a strange person or thing. It is the noun built on odd with -ity.
entries.definitionCN: 怪人；怪事。它是由 odd 加 -ity 构成的名词。

entries.definition: unusual and hard to explain. It is the broad word, while odd often adds a touch of unease or mild humour.
entries.definitionCN: 不寻常且难以解释。它范围最广，odd 常多一层不安或轻微的调侃。

entries.definition: belonging to one person or thing in a way that stands out. It stresses distinctiveness, while odd stresses not fitting the set.
entries.definitionCN: 独特到显眼。它强调“专属、特别”，odd 强调“不合套组”。

entries.definition: unusual in a way that invites interest rather than unease. It is lighter and more neutral than odd.
entries.definitionCN: 奇特得引人好奇，而非令人不安。它比 odd 更轻、更中性。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Old Norse oddi 'third number', the odd one out, and the fixed phrases odd job, odds and ends and Odd Fellows.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：古诺斯语 oddi“第三个数”、the odd one out，以及固定说法 odd job、odds and ends、Odd Fellows。

normal.en: Old Norse oddi meant the third or additional number, the unit that breaks a tie in a vote.
normal.cn: 古诺斯语 oddi 指第三个数、额外的数，就是投票时打破平票的那一单位。

normal.en: A set works by pairs, so whatever cannot be paired is the odd one out.
normal.cn: 一套东西靠成对成立，配不上对的就是 the odd one out。

normal.en: Odd jobs are jobs that belong to no regular set; they are scattered and unpaired.
normal.cn: odd jobs 是不属于任何固定套组的活，零散而不成对。

normal.en: Odds and ends keeps the 'unequal remainder' idea: the scraps that no longer complete anything.
normal.cn: odds and ends 保留“不相等余数”的观念：再也凑不成完整东西的边角料。

normal.en: The arithmetic sense is the oldest: 1, 3, 5 are odd because one is always left over.
normal.cn: 算术义最古老：1、3、5 是奇数，因为每次都余下一个。

abstract.en: Picture three stones on a table: two can be paired, the third sits alone with a sharp corner showing.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上三块石头：两块能配上对，第三块孤零零待着，露出一个尖角。

abstract.en: The lone stone is arithmetic first, then a single glove, then a job that fits no schedule.
abstract.cn: 这块孤石先是算术，再是一只单手套，再是一份不合日程的零工。

abstract.en: When the lone stone is a person, the set's eyes turn on it, and 'left out' becomes 'strange'.
abstract.cn: 当孤石是一个人的时候，整套东西的目光都转向他，“落单”就变成了“古怪”。

examples.en: The street has odd numbers on one side and even numbers on the other.
examples.cn: 这条街一侧是奇数门牌，另一侧是偶数门牌。

examples.en: It seemed odd that such a careful man had left his bag on the train.
examples.cn: 这么细心的一个人竟把包落在火车上，显得很奇怪。

examples.en: She spent the afternoon sorting odds and ends in the bottom drawer.
examples.cn: 她花了一个下午整理最底层抽屉里的零碎东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥德」——奥德洗完衣服只剩一只袜子，又单又怪 → odd 单数的、落单的、古怪的

root: 源自约 1300 年的古诺斯语 oddi“第三个数、额外的数”，字面又指“土地的一角、尖角”，经 oddr“武器尖端”追到原始日耳曼语 *uzdaz“朝上的尖”；从“尖点”到“第三个数”这一步一般认为来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of odd all start from one picture: a unit that cannot be paired. That leftover then becomes an odd number, a single glove, a scattered job, a person set apart, a rough count, and finally the feeling of strangeness.
sensesIntro.cn: odd 的九个义项都从同一幅画出发：一个无法配对成双的单位。这个余数随后变成奇数、单只手套、零散活计、被排除在外的人、粗略的约数，最后变成“古怪”的感觉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one extra unit standing alone beside a matched pair.
core.cn: 核心意象：一对配好的东西旁边，多出一个独自站着的单位。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: the oldest branch, where one is always left over after pairing.
branches.cn: 数目：最古老的分支，两两配对后总会余下一。

branches.en: THE EXTRA UNIT: a single glove, a count a little past the round number, and the scraps that complete nothing.
branches.cn: 多出的单位：单只手套、略超整数的数目，以及凑不成任何东西的边角料。

branches.en: THE IRREGULAR: work and moments that belong to no fixed set and come only now and then.
branches.cn: 不规律：不属于固定套组、只是偶尔出现的工作与时刻。

branches.en: SET APART: the one a group cannot pair with, which draws attention, looks strange, and gives the Odd Fellows their name.
branches.cn: 被排除在外：群体配不上的那一个，它招来注意、显得古怪，也给 Odd Fellows 提供了名字。

branches.en: THE ODDs: unequal numbers turned into a measure of chance and betting.
branches.cn: 赔率：把不相等的数变成机会与赌博的量度。

intro.en: Odd is a bare Norse root with no living English prefix. English builds oddity with -ity and odds with the plural -s, and joins it into compounds such as oddball and odd-looking.
intro.cn: odd 是光秃的诺斯语词根，没有活的英语前缀。英语用 -ity 构成 oddity，用复数 -s 构成 odds，并把它并入 oddball、odd-looking 一类复合词。

latinIntro.en: Odd has no Latin source. Its recorded path is Old Norse oddi and, deeper, Proto-Germanic *uzdaz; the two entries below give those older forms rather than Latin words.
latinIntro.cn: odd 没有拉丁语来源。它的记录路径是古诺斯语 oddi，更深处是原始日耳曼语 *uzdaz；下面两条给出这些更早的形式，而不是拉丁词。

items.structure: odd (bare adjective from Old Norse oddi)
items.meaningCN: 奇数的；不成对的；零星的；古怪的

items.meaning: in a strange or unexpected way
items.meaningCN: 奇怪地；出乎意料地（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 房间里安静得有些奇怪。

items.meaningCN: 奇怪；古怪（-ness 构成状态名词）
items.example: There was an oddness about the whole arrangement.
items.exampleCN: 整个安排透着一种古怪。

items.meaningCN: 怪人；怪事；古怪之处（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The museum is full of mechanical oddities.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆里满是奇巧的机械装置。

items.example: Her oddball uncle kept a boat in the garden.
items.exampleCN: 她那古怪的叔叔在花园里放了一条船。

items.meaning: a leftover piece; a miscellaneous item
items.meaningCN: 零头；残余物；零星物品（-ment 构成名词）
items.example: A box of oddments sat on the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 架子上放着一盒零碎东西。

items.meaningCN: 可能性；赔率；零碎杂物（复数形式）
items.example: The odds of rain tomorrow are high.
items.exampleCN: 明天下雨的可能性很大。

items.meaningCN: 样子古怪的（复合形容词）
items.example: An odd-looking parcel arrived by post.
items.exampleCN: 一个样子古怪的包裹寄到了。

latinEntries.meaning: a third or additional number; point of land, angle
latinEntries.meaningCN: 第三个数、额外的数；土地的一角、尖角（古诺斯语）

definition_zh: 罪行；违法行为；冒犯；得罪；犯规；进攻
definition_en: an illegal act or crime; also the act of upsetting someone, a breaking of the rules in sport, and the attacking side in a game
core_image: 一句话像石子打在别人身上，留下看不见的伤痕
scene: 饭桌上有人顺口拿别人的口音打趣，笑声刚起，桌边几个人的脸就沉了下来。His harmless joke gave offence to half the people at the table.
sceneCN: 这里 offence 是「冒犯、得罪」（第 2 个义项：使别人感到被冒犯）；句意是他那句自以为无伤大雅的玩笑，让半桌人都觉得受了冒犯。画面里有饭桌、碗筷和突然冷下来的气氛。

pos.zh: 罪行；违法行为；冒犯；犯规；进攻

derivatives.zh: 由同族动词 offend 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「犯罪者；违法者」
由同一拉丁词干加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「冒犯的；进攻的」
由 offensive 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「冒犯性；令人反感的程度」

senses.title: An illegal act; a crime
senses.definition: an act that is forbidden by law and can be punished by the state
senses.definitionCN: 法律禁止、可由国家加以惩罚的行为
senses.example: Driving without insurance is a serious offence.
senses.exampleCN: 无保险驾驶是一项严重违法行为。
senses.why: Latin offensa named a striking against something, and English narrowed that image to a wrong the law can punish.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 offensa 本指「撞上、触犯」，英语把这幅画面收窄为法律可以惩罚的过错。

senses.title: The act of upsetting someone
senses.definition: the feeling of being insulted, or the act of saying something that hurts someone
senses.definitionCN: 被人侮辱的感受，或说出使人受伤的话这一行为
senses.example: She took offence at his remark about her accent.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿她的口音开玩笑，她为此生了气。
senses.why: If a word can name a blow, it can also name the sting left by a careless remark, so the same noun covers social injury.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能指一次打击，也就能指一句无心之言留下的刺痛，所以同一个名词也覆盖人情上的伤害。

senses.title: A breaking of the rules in sport
senses.definition: an action that breaks the rules of a game and is punished by the referee
senses.definitionCN: 违反比赛规则、由裁判加以处罚的动作
senses.example: The referee stopped play for a handball offence.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判因手球犯规中止了比赛。
senses.why: A game is a small legal system, so the legal sense of a punishable wrong transfers easily to the pitch.
senses.whyCN: 球赛是一套小型的规则体系，法律上「可受罚的过错」这层意思很自然就挪到了球场上。

senses.title: The attacking side or attacking play
senses.definition: the part of a team or of a game that attacks, as opposed to defence
senses.definitionCN: 一支球队或一场比赛中负责进攻的一方，与防守相对
senses.example: Their offence moved the ball quickly up the left side.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的进攻沿着左路快速推进。
senses.why: The word already carries the image of moving against something, so a team pushing forward is called the offence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本来就带着「朝着某物撞过去」的画面，所以向前推进的一方被称作进攻。

intro.en: Offence is the noun of a Latin verb for striking against, and it reached English through French with both a legal and a personal sense.
intro.cn: offence 是拉丁语中「撞上去」这一动词的名词形式，经法语进入英语，同时带来法律与人情两层含义。

items.en: The verb offendere was built from ob-, meaning against, and fendere, meaning to strike, so it pictured a blow aimed at something.
items.cn: 动词 offendere 由表示「对着、朝向」的 ob- 与表示「打击」的 fendere 构成，画面是朝着某物打过去的一击。

items.en: The noun offensa grew from that verb and meant a striking against, an obstacle, and a wrong that had been committed.
items.cn: 名词 offensa 从这一动词长出，指撞上、障碍，以及已经犯下的过错。

items.en: Old French passed the noun on as offense, keeping both the legal sense of a wrong and the sense of being insulted.
items.cn: 古法语把这一名词写作 offense 传入，既保留「过错」的法律义，也保留「被冒犯」的感受义。

items.en: Middle English offence covered crimes, sins and personal slights, and the spelling settled with a c before i.
items.cn: 中古英语的 offence 同时指罪行、罪过和人情上的冒犯，拼写在 i 之前逐渐固定为 c。

items.en: British English keeps offence while American English writes offense, the form closer to Latin offensa.
items.cn: 现代英式英语保留 offence，美式英语写作 offense，后者更接近拉丁语 offensa 的拼法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the verb, the American spelling and the word family built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers legal and social words for wrongdoing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的动词、美式拼写与词族；近义组收法律与人情两方面表示过错的词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, meaning to upset someone or to commit a crime.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词，义为冒犯别人或犯罪。

entries.definition: The American spelling of offence, used for the same crime and the same insult.
entries.definitionCN: offence 的美式拼写，所指的罪行与冒犯完全相同。

entries.definition: An adjective and noun built on the same stem, meaning insulting or used for attack.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上的形容词兼名词，义为冒犯的或用于进攻的。

entries.definition: A person who commits an offence or breaks the law.
entries.definitionCN: 犯下罪行或违法的人。

entries.definition: An act forbidden by law and punishable by the state.
entries.definitionCN: 法律禁止并可由国家惩处的行为。

entries.definition: An act of breaking a rule, a law or an agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 违反规则、法律或约定的行为。

entries.definition: A rude remark or action that wounds someone's dignity.
entries.definitionCN: 伤害他人尊严的无礼言语或举动。

entries.definition: Behaviour that is illegal or morally unacceptable.
entries.definitionCN: 违法或在道德上不可接受的行为。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin stem for striking, and its family keeps returning to blows that land on people, rules and laws.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「打击」的拉丁词干上，同族词反复回到落在人、规则与法律上的那一击。

normal.en: Latin fendere means to strike, and ob- means against, so offence is literally a blow aimed at someone.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 fendere 意为打击，ob- 意为对着，所以 offence 字面上就是朝人打出的一击。

normal.en: Offence and offend are one family: the verb is the blow, the noun is the blow and the wrong it leaves.
normal.cn: offence 与 offend 同属一族：动词是那一击，名词既是这一击，也是它留下的过错。

normal.en: British spelling keeps the c, American spelling writes offense, which is closer to Latin offensa.
normal.cn: 英式拼写保留 c，美式写作 offense，更接近拉丁语 offensa。

normal.en: Take offence means to treat another person's words as a blow aimed at you.
normal.cn: take offence 意为「见怪」，就是把他人的话当成朝自己打来的一击。

normal.en: Criminal offence stretches the same word from a rude remark all the way to a punishable crime.
normal.cn: criminal offence 把同一个词从一句失礼的话一直拉到可受惩罚的罪行。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence thrown like a stone across a dinner table: the bruise is invisible, but offence is its name.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话像石头一样越过饭桌扔过来：伤痕看不见，而 offence 就是这道伤的名字。

abstract.en: One step over the white line on a pitch is an offence, and so is one step over the line of politeness.
abstract.cn: 球场上越过白线一步是犯规，越过礼貌的界线一步也是冒犯。

abstract.en: The same noun covers a rude word and a crime, which shows that harm is only a matter of degree.
abstract.cn: 同一个名词既指一句无礼的话，也指一桩罪行，说明伤害只是程度之差。

examples.en: Driving without insurance is a serious offence.
examples.cn: 无保险驾驶是一项严重违法行为。

examples.en: She took offence at his remark about her accent.
examples.cn: 他拿她的口音开玩笑，她为此生了气。

examples.en: Their offence was too slow to break the defence.
examples.cn: 他们的进攻太慢，打不穿对方的防线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，犯事」——哦，犯事了，就是 offence：失礼也好，犯罪也好，都是犯了事。

root: 拉丁语 offendere（撞上、触犯）由 ob-（对着）加 fendere（打击）构成；名词 offensa 经古法语 offense 进入英语，英式写作 offence，美式写作 offense。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a blow that lands where it should not; from there the word divides into crime, personal insult, a sporting foul and attacking play.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「落在不该落之处的一击」；由此分出罪行、人情冒犯、体育犯规与进攻一方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a careless word crossing the table like a small stone and hitting someone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句无心的话像小石子一样越过桌面，打在别人身上。

branches.en: a charge read aloud in a courtroom
branches.cn: 法庭上被宣读的一条罪名

branches.en: a foot over the white line and a referee's whistle
branches.cn: 一只脚越过白线，裁判吹响哨子

branches.en: a joke that makes a dinner table go quiet
branches.cn: 一句玩笑让整张饭桌安静下来

branches.en: a team pushing all its players into the other half
branches.cn: 球队把全部球员压到对方半场

branches.en: one crossing of the line, slight as rudeness or heavy as crime
branches.cn: 同一次越界，轻则失礼，重则犯罪

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin prefix of direction, a Latin root for striking, its verb and noun, and two English suffixes for the wrong and the person who does it.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示方向的拉丁前缀、表示打击的拉丁词根、它们的动词与名词，以及两个分别指「过错」和「做此事的人」的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a person who commits an offence

definition_zh: 冒犯；得罪；使不快；犯罪；违法；违反；触犯；使感官不适
definition_en: to make someone feel upset or insulted; to commit a crime or break a rule; to be unpleasant to the senses
core_image: 伸出的手没有握成拳，却仍不小心撞到了别人
scene: 一句关于口音的玩笑刚出口，原本热闹的聚会忽然安静，几个人低头不再说话。His joke about her hometown offended several guests at the party.
sceneCN: 这里 offend 是「冒犯、使不快」（第 1 个义项：使别人感到被冒犯）；句意是他拿她家乡开的玩笑，让聚会上好几位客人不快。画面里是一群围坐的人，笑声突然停住。

pos.zh: 冒犯；得罪；犯罪；违反；触犯；使感官不适

derivatives.zh: 由 offend 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「犯罪者；违法者」
由同一拉丁词干加名词后缀 -ce 构成，义为「罪行；冒犯」（英式拼写）
由 offend 的拉丁词干加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「冒犯的；进攻的」
由 offend 加 -ing 构成，作定语表示「令人反感的；造成问题的」

senses.title: To make someone feel upset or insulted
senses.definition: to say or do something that hurts someone's feelings or insults them
senses.definitionCN: 说出或做出伤害别人感情、使人受辱的话或事
senses.example: His joke offended several guests at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 他那个玩笑得罪了聚会上的好几位客人。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to strike against, and a remark can strike a person just as a blow can.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「撞上」，而一句话也能像一拳那样撞到人身上。

senses.title: To commit a crime or a wrong
senses.definition: to commit a crime or do something morally wrong
senses.definitionCN: 犯下罪行，或做出道德上错误的事
senses.example: He offended repeatedly before he was finally caught.
senses.exampleCN: 他屡次作案，最终才被抓。
senses.why: Offendere also meant to stumble or to transgress, and English kept that sense for breaking a law or a moral code.
senses.whyCN: offendere 也有「失足、越界」的意思，英语保留了这层，用来指触犯法律或道德规范。

senses.title: To break a rule or principle
senses.definition: to go against a rule, a principle or a standard
senses.definitionCN: 违背某条规则、原则或标准
senses.example: The new policy offends against the principle of equal pay.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策违反了同工同酬的原则。
senses.why: With against, the verb points the blow at an abstract standard rather than a person, so the insult turns into a violation.
senses.whyCN: 接上 against 时，这一击指向的不再是人，而是一条抽象标准，于是「冒犯」转为「违反」。

senses.title: To be unpleasant to the senses
senses.definition: to be offensive to the eye, the ear or the nose
senses.definitionCN: 使眼睛、耳朵或鼻子感到不适
senses.example: The bright green paint offends the eye in that quiet room.
senses.exampleCN: 在那间素净的屋子里，那面亮绿色的墙看着很扎眼。
senses.why: Since a blow can land on the body, the same verb can describe what jars the senses, which is the last step from people to eyes and noses.
senses.whyCN: 既然一击能落在人身上，同一个动词也能形容刺到感官的东西，这就是从人走到眼睛与鼻子的最后一步。

intro.en: Offend is a Latin verb for striking against that came through French, and its sense moved from stumbling and sinning to hurting feelings.
intro.cn: offend 是拉丁语中表示「撞上去」的动词，经法语进入英语，词义从失足、犯罪一路走到伤害感情。

items.en: Offendere joined ob-, meaning against, with fendere, meaning to strike, so its first picture was a blow aimed at something.
items.cn: offendere 把表示「对着」的 ob- 与表示「打击」的 fendere 合在一起，最初的画面是朝着某物打出一击。

items.en: In Latin the verb also meant to stumble against an obstacle and to transgress, which prepared the later moral senses.
items.cn: 在拉丁语中，这个动词还表示撞上障碍、失足，以及越界，这为后来的道德义埋下了伏笔。

items.en: Old French offendre meant to wrong or to sin, and it supplied English with the verb in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 古法语 offendre 意为冒犯或犯罪，中世纪时把这个动词送进了英语。

items.en: Middle English offenden first meant to sin or to transgress, and only later came to mean to displease a person.
items.cn: 中古英语的 offenden 最初指犯罪、越界，后来才引申为使人不快。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the legal sense of breaking a rule and the everyday sense of hurting someone's feelings.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留「违反规则」的法律义与「伤害感情」的日常义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun and adjectives of the same Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for hurting feelings and breaking rules.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词族的名词与形容词；近义组收表示伤人感情与违反规则的动词。

entries.definitionCN: 表示罪行或冒犯行为的英式名词。

entries.definitionCN: 与 offend 相关的名词的美式拼写。

entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上的形容词兼名词，义为冒犯的或进攻的。

entries.definitionCN: 冒犯他人或违反法律的人。

entries.definition: To make someone feel unhappy, worried or annoyed.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人感到不快、担心或恼火。

entries.definition: To make someone feel annoyed or not satisfied.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人感到不快或不满意。

entries.definition: To break a law, a rule or an agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 违反法律、规则或约定。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin verb of striking that turned into a family of nouns and adjectives about wrongdoing and wounded feelings.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示打击的动词，后来长成一族指过错与伤人感情的名词与形容词。

normal.en: Ob- plus fendere gives a blow aimed at someone, and that is the physical core of offend.
normal.cn: ob- 加 fendere 就是朝人打出的一击，这就是 offend 的身体性内核。

normal.en: Offend against is the pattern for breaking a law or a principle, not for hurting a person.
normal.cn: offend against 是违反法律或原则的固定搭配，而不是指伤害某个人。

normal.en: Offender adds -er to the verb: the person who lands the blow or commits the crime.
normal.cn: offender 在动词后加 -er，就是打出这一击、犯下罪行的那个人。

normal.en: Be offended by marks the receiver of the blow, the person whose feelings were hurt.
normal.cn: be offended by 标出的是承受一击的一方，也就是感情受伤的人。

normal.en: Offend the eye shows that the verb can strike senses as well as feelings.
normal.cn: offend the eye 说明这个动词不只打击感情，也能打击感官。

abstract.en: Picture a small stone thrown in conversation: it leaves no mark on the skin, but offend names the bruise underneath.
abstract.cn: 想象谈话中扔出的一颗小石子：皮肤上没有痕迹，而 offend 就是底下那块淤青的名字。

abstract.en: A step over a rule touches the law first and someone's feelings second, and one verb covers both.
abstract.cn: 越过规则的那一步，先触到法律，再触到别人的感受，同一个动词把两者都收下了。

abstract.en: Offence is often unintended, yet it still lands on the other person; that gap is what the word keeps alive.
abstract.cn: 冒犯常常不是本意，却仍然落在对方身上；这道落差正是这个词一直保留的东西。

examples.en: His joke offended several guests at the party.
examples.cn: 他那个玩笑得罪了聚会上的好几位客人。

examples.en: The new policy offends against the principle of equal pay.
examples.cn: 新政策违反了同工同酬的原则。

examples.en: Loud colours offend the eye in such a quiet room.
examples.cn: 在这样素净的房间里，刺眼的颜色看着很不舒服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，犯的」——哦，是他犯的；offend 既是冒犯别人，也是犯了事。

root: 拉丁语 offendere（撞上、触犯）由 ob-（对着）加 fendere（打击）构成，经古法语 offendre 进入英语；同族词有 offence、offensive、offender。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a blow aimed at someone; the senses divide into wounded feelings, broken law, broken rule and jarred senses.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「朝人打出的一击」；义项分为受伤的感情、触犯的法律、违反的规则与受刺激的感官。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching out without a fist, still bumping into another person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只没有握成拳的手伸出去，还是撞到了别人。

branches.en: a joke that makes a face at the table go cold
branches.cn: 一句玩笑让桌边一张脸冷下来

branches.en: a man standing in the dock after repeated thefts
branches.cn: 屡次行窃的人站在被告席上

branches.en: a new clause that clashes with an old principle
branches.cn: 新条款与旧原则相抵触

branches.en: harsh light and a sharp smell that make people turn away
branches.cn: 强光与刺鼻气味让人别过脸

branches.en: the same force that wounds a person can also wound an eye
branches.cn: 伤人的那股力，也能伤到一双眼睛

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin prefix of direction, a root for striking, the Latin verb built from them, and two English suffixes for the person and the resulting quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示方向的拉丁前缀、表示打击的词根、由二者构成的拉丁动词，以及分别指「人」和「由此生出的性质」的两个英语后缀支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词词尾
现在分词与动作名词词尾

definition_zh: 冒犯的；无礼的；令人反感的；进攻的；攻势
definition_en: causing someone to feel insulted or upset; extremely unpleasant; used for or taking the attack; as a noun, a planned military attack
core_image: 一句话和一支军队都朝着同一个方向推出去
scene: 看台上有人拉起一条嘲弄对方球队的横幅，周围的笑声很快变成了争吵。The referee warned that the banner was offensive and had to be removed.
sceneCN: 这里 offensive 是「冒犯的、无礼的」（第 1 个义项：使人感到被冒犯）；句意是裁判警告那条横幅带有冒犯意味，必须撤下。画面里有看台、横幅和争执的观众。

pos.zh: 冒犯的；无礼的；令人反感的；进攻的
攻势；进攻

derivatives.zh: 由 offensive 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「冒犯地；进攻性地」
由 offensive 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「冒犯性；令人反感的程度」
由同一拉丁词干 offensa 构成，义为「罪行；冒犯」（英式拼写）
由表示「反」的 counter- 与 offensive 复合而成，义为「反攻」

senses.title: Causing someone to feel insulted
senses.definition: causing someone to feel hurt, angry or insulted
senses.definitionCN: 使别人感到受伤、恼火或受辱的
senses.example: His remarks about her accent were offensive.
senses.exampleCN: 他关于她口音的那些话很冒犯人。
senses.why: The suffix -ive turns the act of striking against into a quality, so words and acts that wound people are called offensive.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ive 把「撞上去」这个动作变成一种性质，于是会伤人的话和行为就被称作冒犯的。

senses.title: Extremely unpleasant to the senses
senses.definition: very unpleasant, especially to see, smell or hear
senses.definitionCN: 尤指在视觉、嗅觉或听觉上非常令人不适的
senses.example: The smell from the drains was offensive.
senses.exampleCN: 下水道里传来的气味很难闻。
senses.why: The blow can land on the senses as well as on feelings, so the adjective also grades what makes the eyes, nose or ears recoil.
senses.whyCN: 这一击不只落在感情上，也落在感官上，所以这个形容词也能形容让眼睛、鼻子或耳朵想要后退的东西。

senses.title: Used for attack; attacking
senses.definition: designed or used for attacking, especially in war or sport
senses.definitionCN: 尤指在战争或体育中为进攻而设计或使用的
senses.example: The soldiers were trained to use offensive weapons.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们受过使用攻击性武器的训练。
senses.why: Because offendere pictured a blow aimed forward, the adjective also names whatever is built to push into the enemy's ground.
senses.whyCN: 因为 offendere 的意象是朝前打出的一击，这个形容词也就用来指一切为推进到对方阵地而准备的东西。

senses.title: A planned military attack
senses.definition: a large organized military attack, or a spell of attacking in a game
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的大规模军事进攻，或比赛中一段持续进攻
senses.example: The spring offensive opened along the whole front.
senses.exampleCN: 春季攻势在整条战线上展开。
senses.why: When the adjective names the attacking mode, it can stand as a noun for the attack itself, so the quality becomes the campaign.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词用来指进攻的方式，它就能独立成名词指进攻本身，性质于是变成了一场战役。

intro.en: Offensive is an adjective built on a Latin participle stem, and it split in English into the insulting, the disgusting and the attacking.
intro.cn: offensive 是建立在拉丁语过去分词词干上的形容词，在英语里分出「冒犯」「令人反感」与「进攻」三路。

items.en: The verb offendere meant to strike against, and its participle stem offens- carried the idea of something that has hit a target.
items.cn: 动词 offendere 意为撞上，其过去分词词干 offens- 带着「已经击中目标」的意思。

items.en: Medieval Latin offensivus, commonly derived from that stem, meant hurtful or ready to strike.
items.cn: 一般认为中世纪拉丁语 offensivus 由这个词干构成，意为会伤人的、动辄要打的。

items.en: Old French offensif took the adjective into French and passed it on to English with the sense of hurtful and attacking.
items.cn: 古法语 offensif 把这个形容词接了过去，再传入英语，带着「会伤人」与「用于进攻」两层意思。

items.en: In English the adjective grew two branches, one for insulting words and one for weapons, and the noun later named a military push.
items.cn: 在英语里这个形容词长出两支，一支指无礼的话，一支指武器，名词后来则用来指一次军事推进。

items.en: Modern English uses offensive for rude remarks, for disgusting smells, and for the attacking side in war and sport.
items.cn: 现代英语用 offensive 指无礼的话、恶心的气味，以及战争与体育中进攻的一方。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun and verb behind this adjective; the near-meaning group gathers words for insult, disgust and attack.
note.cn: 形近组收这个形容词背后的名词与动词；近义组收表示侮辱、反感与进攻的词。

entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁词干上表示罪行或冒犯的名词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the noun from the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上名词的美式拼写。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to insult someone or to break a rule.

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in an insulting or attacking way.
entries.definitionCN: 表示以冒犯或进攻的方式的副词。

entries.definition: Rude and likely to humiliate the person addressed.
entries.definitionCN: 粗鲁并可能使对方受辱的。

entries.definition: Showing little respect for other people.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人缺少尊重的。

entries.definition: So unpleasant that it causes strong dislike.
entries.definitionCN: 极其令人厌恶的。

entries.definition: A planned attempt to defeat an enemy or an opponent.
entries.definitionCN: 为击败敌人或对手而计划发动的进攻。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the Latin stem for striking, and it keeps the same forward push whether the target is a person, a nose or an army.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示打击的拉丁词干上，无论目标是个人、鼻子还是一支军队，它都保持同一个向前的推力。

normal.en: Offend plus -ive makes a quality: what is offensive has the habit of striking people.
normal.cn: offend 加 -ive 构成一种性质：会冒犯的东西带着「打到人」的习性。

normal.en: The same adjective serves for rude remarks and for attacking weapons, because both push forward.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词既修饰无礼的话，也修饰进攻的武器，因为两者都朝前推。

normal.en: Take the offensive turns the adjective into a noun phrase for going on the attack.
normal.cn: take the offensive 把形容词变成名词性短语，表示转为进攻。

normal.en: Offensiveness adds -ness to the adjective and names the quality itself.
normal.cn: offensiveness 在形容词后加 -ness，直接指这种性质本身。

normal.en: Offensive weapon is a legal phrase for something built or used to hurt people.
normal.cn: offensive weapon 是法律用语，指为伤人而制作或使用的物件。

abstract.en: A rude sentence and an advancing army share one direction: both are pushed outward, and both make people step back.
abstract.cn: 一句无礼的话与一支推进的军队共享一个方向：都向外推，也都让人后退。

abstract.en: Offensive smell arrives before words do; the nose is hit before anyone has spoken.
abstract.cn: 令人反感的气味先于语言到达；还没人开口，鼻子已经被击中。

abstract.en: The suffix -ive turns a blow into a tendency, a readiness to keep pushing against whatever is in front.
abstract.cn: 后缀 -ive 把一次打击变成一种倾向，一种不断朝前方顶撞的劲头。

examples.en: His remarks about her accent were offensive.
examples.cn: 他关于她口音的那些话很冒犯人。

examples.en: The smell from the drains was offensive.
examples.cn: 下水道里传来的气味很难闻。

examples.en: The spring offensive opened along the whole front.
examples.cn: 春季攻势在整条战线上展开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，芬西服」——哦，那套芬兰西服穿得怪，让人反感；offensive 就是冒犯的、进攻的。

root: 拉丁语 offendere（撞上、触犯）的过去分词词干 offens- 加 -ive 构成 offensivus，经古法语 offensif 进入英语；同一词干还生出 offence 与 offend。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the forward push of a blow; the adjective splits into insult, disgust and attack, and the noun names the attack itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一击向前的推力」；形容词分出冒犯、反感与进攻，名词则指进攻本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence and an army pushing out in the same direction.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话与一支军队朝同一个方向推出去。

branches.en: a mocking remark about someone's accent
branches.cn: 一句拿别人口音取笑的话

branches.en: a smell by the rubbish bins that stops conversation
branches.cn: 垃圾桶边的气味让人停住话头

branches.en: a weapon built only for hurting people
branches.cn: 只为伤人而制造的武器

branches.en: an attack opened in spring across a long front
branches.cn: 春天在漫长战线上发起的进攻

branches.en: one force that makes people step back, in words or in air
branches.cn: 同一种让人后退的力量，或在言语，或在空气里

intro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb of striking, its participle stem, and an adjectival suffix that turns the act into a lasting quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示打击的拉丁动词、它的过去分词词干，以及把动作变成持久性质的后缀共同构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: having the nature of, tending to
in an insulting or attacking way

items.meaningCN: 构成表示性质的抽象名词

definition_zh: 提供；给予；主动提出；出价；提议；报价；特价
definition_en: to give or present something to someone; to say you are willing to do something; to name a price; as a noun, a proposal, a bid or a special deal
core_image: 双手把东西捧到别人面前，等对方伸手接下
scene: 公交车上人挨着人，一位老人扶着扶手晃了一下，靠窗的年轻人抬手指了指自己旁边的空位。She offered her seat to the old man and he took it with a nod.
sceneCN: 这里 offer 是「提供、让出」（第 1 个义项：把东西给予别人）；句意是她把座位让给了老人，老人点头接受。画面里有拥挤的车厢和一个靠窗的空位。

pos.zh: 提供；给予；主动提出；出价
提议；报价；录用通知；特价

derivatives.zh: 由 offer 加 -ing 构成，义为「献上的东西；祭品；提供的服务或课程」
法律用语，由 offer 加表示「人」的后缀 -or 构成，义为「提出要约的一方」
源自拉丁 offertorium，与 offer 同一词根，义为「礼拜中的奉献环节或奉献金」

senses.title: To give or present something to someone
senses.definition: to give something to someone, especially in a polite or formal way
senses.definitionCN: 尤指以礼貌或正式的方式把某物给予别人
senses.example: She offered him a cup of tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她给他端来一杯茶。
senses.why: Latin offerre meant to bring something before a person, and that picture of presenting an object still drives the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 offerre 意为把东西带到某人面前，这幅「捧到人前」的画面一直支撑着第一个义项。

senses.title: To say that you are willing to do something
senses.definition: to express willingness to do something for someone
senses.definitionCN: 向别人表示自己愿意做某事
senses.example: He offered to drive us to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他主动提出开车送我们去车站。
senses.why: Once the thing brought forward can be an action rather than an object, the verb comes to mean putting yourself forward as willing.
senses.whyCN: 当被捧到人前的不再是物件而是一个行动，这个动词就引申为「把自己递上去」，表示愿意效劳。

senses.title: To name a price for something
senses.definition: to say what price you will pay for something or charge for it
senses.definitionCN: 说出你愿意为某物支付、或为某物开出的价钱
senses.example: They offered two million for the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们出价两百万买那栋房子。
senses.why: In a market the thing brought forward is a sum of money, so presenting turns into bidding.
senses.whyCN: 在市场里，被捧到人前的变成一笔钱，于是「呈上」就转成了「出价」。

senses.title: A proposal or a job offer
senses.definition: a formal proposal, especially one made to be accepted or refused
senses.definitionCN: 正式的提议，尤指摆出来等对方接受或拒绝的那种
senses.example: The company made her an offer she could not refuse.
senses.exampleCN: 公司给了她一个无法拒绝的录用条件。
senses.why: The noun keeps the object that was brought forward, so an offer is the proposal itself, waiting for a yes or a no.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了那个被捧出来的东西，所以 an offer 就是摆在面前、等人点头或摇头的提议。

senses.title: A special price or deal
senses.definition: a reduced price or a deal advertised to attract buyers
senses.definitionCN: 为吸引买家而宣传的降价价格或优惠方案
senses.example: The shop has a special offer on coffee this week.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店本周咖啡有特价。
senses.why: When a price is put in front of a buyer as a bargain, the same noun narrows to the attractive deal on the label.
senses.whyCN: 当价格作为便宜货摆到买家面前，同一个名词就收窄为标签上那个吸引人的优惠。

intro.en: Offer goes back to a Latin verb meaning to bring before, was borrowed early into Old English for sacrifice, and was then widened by French to any kind of presenting.
intro.cn: offer 可追到拉丁语中意为「带到面前」的动词，早期借入古英语时指献祭，后经法语扩展为一切形式的呈上。

items.en: Offerre joined ob-, meaning toward or before, with ferre, meaning to bring, so it meant to bring something before someone.
items.cn: offerre 把表示「向前、对着」的 ob- 与表示「带来、搬运」的 ferre 合在一起，意为把东西带到某人面前。

items.en: Old English borrowed the Latin verb early as offrian, and its first use was bringing a sacrifice before God.
items.cn: 古英语早期就把这个拉丁动词借进来写作 offrian，最初用于把祭品献到神面前。

items.en: Norman French offrir reinforced the word and widened it from sacrifice to any act of presenting.
items.cn: 诺曼法语 offrir 重新加固了这个词，并把「献祭」扩展为任何形式的呈上。

items.en: Middle English offer covered presenting gifts, making a proposal and naming a price.
items.cn: 中古英语的 offer 已覆盖呈上礼物、提出建议与开出价钱。

items.en: Modern English keeps the religious echo in offering and offertory, and the commercial sense in bid and special offer.
items.cn: 现代英语在 offering 与 offertory 里保留宗教余音，在出价与特价里保留商业含义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derivatives and other words built on the Latin verb for carrying; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for giving, proposing and bidding.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词以及同样建立在拉丁语「搬运」动词上的词；近义组收表示给予、提议与出价的动词。

entries.definition: Something presented, especially to a god or to a fund.
entries.definitionCN: 献上的东西，尤指献神或捐献之物。

entries.definition: The part of a church service when gifts are collected.
entries.definitionCN: 礼拜中收集奉献的环节。

entries.definition: To send a matter or a person to another source, built on the Latin verb for carrying.
entries.definitionCN: 把事务或人转到另一处，建立在拉丁语「搬运」动词上。

entries.definition: To move something from one place to another, with the same carrying root.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从一处移到另一处，共享同一个「搬运」词根。

entries.definition: To give or hand something to someone, often formally.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物给予或递交某人，常用于正式场合。

entries.definition: To suggest a plan or an idea for others to consider.
entries.definitionCN: 提出计划或想法供他人考虑。

entries.definition: An offer of a particular amount of money for something.
entries.definitionCN: 为某物开出的某个数目的价钱。

entries.definition: To give someone something they need.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人提供其需要的东西。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb for bringing something forward, and its family keeps the picture of a gift placed in front of another person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语「把东西向前带」的动词上，同族词始终保留「把礼物摆到别人面前」的画面。

normal.en: Offerre is ob- plus ferre, so the word pictures someone bringing an object forward into view.
normal.cn: offerre 是 ob- 加 ferre，画面就是有人把东西向前带到别人眼前。

normal.en: Old English offrian first meant to sacrifice, which is why offering still sounds religious.
normal.cn: 古英语 offrian 最初指献祭，所以 offering 至今还带宗教味道。

normal.en: Offering adds -ing to offer and names the thing that was placed before someone.
normal.cn: offering 在 offer 后加 -ing，指那个被摆到人前的东西。

normal.en: Offer to do takes an infinitive and marks willingness rather than an object.
normal.cn: offer to do 后面接不定式，标出的是意愿，而不是一件物件。

normal.en: On offer is the British phrase for goods that are available or reduced in price.
normal.cn: on offer 是英式说法，指商品可买到或正在减价。

abstract.en: Picture both hands holding something out at arm's length, waiting for the other person to reach back.
abstract.cn: 想象双手把东西捧出一臂远，等着对方也伸出手来。

abstract.en: A bid is money pushed onto the table, and the other side still has to nod.
abstract.cn: 出价就是把钱推到桌面上，另一头还得点头才行。

abstract.en: Offering help means extending a hand before anyone asks for it.
abstract.cn: 主动帮忙，就是在别人开口之前先把手伸出去。

examples.en: She offered her seat to the old man.
examples.cn: 她把座位让给了那位老人。

examples.en: He offered to drive us to the station.
examples.cn: 他主动提出开车送我们去车站。

examples.en: The company made her an offer she could not refuse.
examples.cn: 公司给了她一个无法拒绝的录用条件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，发了」——哦，发了笔财，是因为有人给你出了个好价；offer 就是提供与出价。

root: 拉丁语 offerre（带到面前）由 ob-（向前、对着）加 ferre（带来、搬运）构成，古英语早期借入作 offrian 表示献祭，又经古法语 offrir 加固；同族词有 offering、offertory。

sensesIntro.en: The core is bringing something before a person; the senses divide into giving, volunteering, naming a price, a proposal and a bargain.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把东西带到人面前」；义项分为给予、主动提出、出价、提议与优惠。

core.cn: 核心意象：双手把一件东西捧向另一个人。

branches.cn: 一杯茶被轻轻推到桌子对面

branches.en: a man saying he will drive everyone home
branches.cn: 一个人说愿意开车送大家回家

branches.en: a price written on a card beside a house
branches.cn: 房子旁卡片上写着一个价格

branches.en: a proposal and a letter of employment laid on a desk
branches.cn: 摊在桌上的提案与录用信

branches.en: a bright label in a shop window
branches.cn: 商店橱窗里醒目的标签

intro.cn: 这个词由表示方向的拉丁前缀、表示搬运的拉丁动词、二者构成的复合动词，以及分别指「动作」和「所献之物」的英语后缀共同支撑。

place or thing connected with an action
