definition_zh: 正式地；官方地；据官方说法；以公职身份
definition_en: in a way that comes from or is approved by an authority, in one's formal public role, according to the public record, or by due formal procedure
core_image: 一枚刻着徽记的印章落在文件末页，红色的印痕慢慢干透
scene: 清晨的会议室里，长桌两端坐满人，秘书把盖好章的公告放进文件夹，等时间一到就发出去。The new rules were officially announced on Monday morning.
sceneCN: 这里的 officially 是「正式地、由官方宣布」（第 1 个义项：经权威渠道公布）；句意为新规定在星期一上午正式宣布。图中可辨识物件：长桌、公告、印章。

pos.zh: 正式地；官方地；以公职身份

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 officium（职务、义务）经法语进入英语，义为「官方的；正式的」
由 official 加 -dom 构成，义为「官僚；官场」
由 official 与 -ese 构成，指公文里常见的「官样腔调」

senses.title: Announced or approved by an authority
senses.definition: in a way that is stated, approved or confirmed by a person or body holding authority
senses.definitionCN: 由掌握权威的人或机构宣布、批准或确认的方式
senses.example: The results were officially announced on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 结果在星期五正式公布。
senses.why: The Latin noun officium named a duty attached to a post, so what is officially said is what someone with a post has the right to declare.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 officium 指附在职位上的职责，因此 officially 说出的，就是有职位的人有权宣布的内容，词的重点落在「谁有权说」。

senses.title: In one's public role or capacity
senses.definition: as part of one's public duties rather than as a private person
senses.definitionCN: 作为公职职责的一部分，而不是以私人身份行事
senses.example: She was there officially, representing the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 她是以公职身份到场的，代表的是那个部门。
senses.why: Because officium also named the service owed to a position, the adverb marks the capacity in which a person acts rather than the private person.
senses.whyCN: officium 也指一个职位所应尽的差事，所以这个副词标的是一个人以何种身份行事，而不是他作为私人是谁。

senses.title: According to the public record, though perhaps not in fact
senses.definition: as reported or recorded in public by officials, often with a hint that the reality may differ
senses.definitionCN: 按官员对外公布或记录的说法，常暗示真实情况可能不同
senses.example: Officially the road is open, but the barrier is still down.
senses.exampleCN: 官方说这条路已经开放，可栏杆还放下来着。
senses.why: A claim that carries the stamp of an office is only the version on record, and speakers use officially to set that version against what they can see for themselves.
senses.whyCN: 带官印的说法只是记录在案的那一版，于是人们用 officially 把这一版和自己亲眼所见对起来，话里常藏着怀疑。

senses.title: By due formal procedure
senses.definition: in a formal or legal way, following the steps required for a change to count
senses.definitionCN: 以正式或合法的方式，走完让一项变动生效所需的手续
senses.example: He officially resigned at the end of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 他在月底正式辞职。
senses.why: If a post is what makes an act official, then an act becomes final only when the proper steps are closed, and the adverb names that closing step.
senses.whyCN: 既然职位使一个举动成为官方举动，那么这个举动只有在手续走完时才算落定，副词指的正是这最后一步。

intro.en: Officially is the adverb of official, and official reached English from Latin officium by way of French; the whole family keeps the idea of a duty tied to a post.
intro.cn: officially 是 official 的副词，而 official 由拉丁语 officium 经法语进入英语；这一族词始终围绕「附在职位上的职责」这个意思。

items.en: Officium meant a duty, a service or the work attached to a public post, and it joined ops, wealth or power, with the verb facere, to do.
items.cn: officium 指职责、服务或附在公职上的事务，一般认为是 ops（财力、权力）与动词 facere（做）结合而成。

items.en: Officialis described what belonged to a magistrate or to a duty, and it passed into French as a word for an office holder and for what such a person does.
items.cn: officialis 形容属于长官或职务的事物，进入法语后既指任职者，也指这类人所办的事。

items.en: Old French officiel carried the sense of what is publicly authorized, and English borrowed it with that stamp of authority intact.
items.cn: 古法语 officiel 带着「经公开授权」的意思，英语借入时把这层权威印记一并保留。

items.en: Middle English used official for church officers and for things said by authority, and -ly later turned it into an adverb of manner.
items.cn: 中古英语用 official 指教会官员和由权威说出的事，后来 -ly 把它变成方式副词。

items.en: Modern English adds officially to announcements, to the capacity in which someone acts, to public claims that may be doubted, and to steps that make a change final.
items.cn: 现代英语把 officially 用在公告、行事身份、可能存疑的公开说法，以及让变动生效的程序步骤上。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem for duty and office; the near-meaning group collects adverbs for public, formal and recorded statement.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在表示「职责、职务」的拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示公开、正式、记录在案的说法副词。

entries.definition: Approved by an authority, or a person who holds a post.
entries.definitionCN: 经权威批准的；也指担任职务的人。

entries.definition: A position of duty, or the room where such work is done.
entries.definitionCN: 职务；也指办理这类工作的房间。

entries.definition: Too eager to give orders or advice that nobody asked for.
entries.definitionCN: 过分热心于发号施令或提建议的。

entries.definition: Officials seen as a group with their own habits and language.
entries.definitionCN: 把官员看作一个有自身习气与话语的群体。

entries.definition: In a way that follows accepted rules or ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 按公认规则或礼仪进行的方式。

entries.definition: Openly, so that anyone may see or hear it.
entries.definitionCN: 公开地，任何人都能看到或听到。

entries.definition: Stated in a way that is written down or can be checked.
entries.definitionCN: 以被写下、可供查证的方式说明。

entries.definition: From someone whose position makes the statement count.
entries.definitionCN: 出自说话有分量、地位使然的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is official wearing -ly, and official is a Latin duty-noun turned adjective, so every hook returns to a post and the rights that come with it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 official 穿上 -ly，而 official 是拉丁语「职责」名词变来的形容词，所以每条记忆钩子都回到职位以及随之而来的权力。

normal.en: Official plus -ly gives officially, the ordinary way English builds a manner adverb from an adjective.
normal.cn: official 加 -ly 得到 officially，这是英语由形容词构成方式副词的常规做法。

normal.en: Officium joined a word for wealth or power with facere, to do, so the core picture is work done because a post requires it.
normal.cn: officium 把表示财力或权力的词与 facere（做）结合起来，核心画面是因职位要求而做的事。

normal.en: Official is also a noun for a person who holds a post, which is why officially can mean 'in that person's capacity'.
normal.cn: official 也可作名词指担任职务的人，所以 officially 能表示「以那个人的身份」。

normal.en: Officially announced and officially opened are fixed pairings: the adverb tells us the source of the approval.
normal.cn: officially announced 与 officially opened 是固定搭配：副词点明批准来自哪里。

normal.en: When a sentence begins with officially, expect a 'but' later; the word often sets the record against the reality.
normal.cn: 句子以 officially 开头时，后面多半有一个「可是」；这个词常把记录与现实并排摆出。

abstract.en: A word built on duty quietly asks who has the right to speak, not just whether the statement is true.
abstract.cn: 一个建立在「职责」上的词，悄悄追问的是谁有权说话，而不只是话是否属实。

abstract.en: The same adverb can mean both 'authorized' and 'merely on paper', which is how official language earns its reputation.
abstract.cn: 同一个副词既能表示「已获授权」，也能表示「只是纸面上」，官方话语的名声正由此而来。

abstract.en: To do something officially is to let a procedure finish the act, as if the last signature did the real work.
abstract.cn: 正式地做一件事，就是让程序来完成这个举动，仿佛真正干活的是最后那个签名。

examples.en: The bridge was officially opened by the mayor.
examples.cn: 这座桥由市长正式启用。

examples.en: Officially she is on holiday, though her phone never stops.
examples.cn: 官方说法是她在休假，可她的电话一直响个不停。

examples.en: The company officially became a charity last spring.
examples.cn: 这家公司去年春天正式成为慈善机构。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿费事里」——盖章办事得跑一趟，费事里透着正式；记住 officially 是正式地。

root: 由 official 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；official 来自拉丁语 officialis，再上溯 officium（职务、义务），一般认为由 ops（财力、权力）与 facere（做）合成。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a duty tied to a post; from it come the authorized announcement, the capacity in which one acts, the record that may be doubted, and the procedure that makes a change final.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是附在职位上的职责；由此分出经授权的宣布、行事的身份、可能存疑的记录，以及让变动生效的程序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal stamped on the last page of a document, its red mark slowly drying.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚刻着徽记的印章落在文件末页，红色的印痕慢慢干透。

branches.en: a sealed notice waiting to be released at nine
branches.cn: 封好印章、等九点才发出的公告

branches.en: a delegate speaking for a ministry, not for herself
branches.cn: 代表部门发言、不代表本人的代表

branches.en: a sign saying open above a locked barrier
branches.cn: 写着开放、栏杆却放下的告示

branches.en: a signature that makes a resignation final
branches.cn: 让辞呈最终生效的签名

branches.en: the same stamp turning words into an effective act
branches.cn: 同一枚印章把话语变成生效的举动

intro.en: The word is a Latin duty-noun that became an adjective and then an adverb; its parts are the noun, its adjective ending, the English adjective and the two endings that extend it.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「职责」名词变成形容词、再变成副词；构件是该名词、它的形容词词尾、英语形容词，以及继续扩展它的两个词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin officium, officialis and officiosus are all recorded, so this family has a reliable Latin ancestry behind its English forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 officium、officialis、officiosus 均有记录，因此这一族英语词形背后有可靠的拉丁语世系。

items.meaning: relating to a duty or magistrate

definition_zh: 抵消；补偿；弥补；对冲；偏移；胶印
definition_en: to balance one cost, effect or influence against another so that the net result is reduced
core_image: 天平一端压着涨价账单，另一端放上节省下来的硬币，横梁慢慢回到水平
scene: 运费涨了不少，但仓库搬到近郊后省下的租金正好填上这块。The savings offset the higher freight cost.
sceneCN: 这里指用省下的钱抵掉多出来的开支（第 1 个义项：抵消成本或开支）；句意为节省的费用抵消了上涨的运费。图中可辨识物件：天平、涨价的账单、一叠硬币。

pos.zh: 抵消；补偿；弥补；对冲
抵消；偏移；胶印

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示进行或性质的后缀构成，义为「抵消；起抵消作用的」
名词复数，义为「各项抵消额；偏移量」
由「碳」与「抵消额」合成的复合词，义为「碳抵消额度」

senses.title: To cancel a cost
senses.definition: to balance an extra cost with a saving elsewhere so that the net charge falls
senses.definitionCN: 用在别处省下的钱抵掉额外开支，使净支出下降
senses.example: The lower rent offset the rise in transport fees.
senses.exampleCN: 更低的租金抵消了运费的上涨。
senses.why: The word pictures one item set against another on a scale, and money is the easiest thing to weigh that way.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的画面是把一项放在天平上与另一项对着，而钱最容易被这样称量。

senses.title: To compensate for a loss
senses.definition: to make up for a loss or disadvantage with a gain in another area
senses.definitionCN: 用另一方面的收益补上损失或劣势
senses.example: Higher output offset the loss of two machines.
senses.exampleCN: 更高的产量补偿了两台机器的损失。
senses.why: Compensation is the accounting face of the same balance: what was lost is entered against what was gained.
senses.whyCN: 补偿是同一平衡的会计面孔：失去的与得到的对着记账。

senses.title: To make up for a shortfall
senses.definition: to supply what is missing so that the total reaches the required level
senses.definitionCN: 补上缺少的部分，使总量达到应有水平
senses.example: Extra tutoring offset the gap in her early schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 额外的辅导弥补了她早期教育的缺口。
senses.why: A shortfall is an imbalance on one side, and the verb puts weight on the other side.
senses.whyCN: 缺口是一侧的不平衡，这个动词往另一侧放上重量。

senses.title: To hedge a risk
senses.definition: to arrange a position that moves opposite to a risk so that losses are limited
senses.definitionCN: 安排一个与风险反向的头寸，以限制损失
senses.example: The airline offset its fuel exposure with forward contracts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司用远期合约对冲燃油敞口。
senses.why: Finance takes the scale literally: two positions are set against each other on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 金融把这个天平照字面使用：两个头寸被有意对着摆。

senses.title: To shift a position
senses.definition: to move an object or a line away from its original centre or alignment
senses.definitionCN: 使物体或线条离开原来的中心或对齐位置
senses.example: The surveyor offset the foundation line by ten centimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 测量员把基础线偏移了十厘米。
senses.why: Printing and engineering use offset for a displacement, the same side-by-side picture moved into space.
senses.whyCN: 印刷与工程用这个词表示位移，即同一「错开摆放」的画面移入空间。

senses.title: To balance the books
senses.definition: to enter one amount against another so that the accounts agree
senses.definitionCN: 把一笔金额对着另一笔记账，使账目相符
senses.example: The auditor offset the advance against the final invoice.
senses.exampleCN: 审计员把预付款与最终发票相抵。
senses.why: Accounting formalised the scale into two columns that must come to the same total.
senses.whyCN: 会计把这个天平固定成两栏，两栏最后要合成同一个数。

senses.title: To print by offset
senses.definition: to print from a plate onto a rubber blanket and then onto paper
senses.definitionCN: 先把印版上的图文转到橡皮布，再转到纸上
senses.example: The booklet was offset on coated stock.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小册子用胶印印在铜版纸上。
senses.why: The printing sense grew from the idea of an indirect transfer, ink being set off onto another surface.
senses.whyCN: 印刷义从「间接转移」长出，油墨被「转印」到另一表面。

senses.title: To neutralise emissions
senses.definition: to remove or balance an amount of carbon or pollution by an equivalent saving elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 用在别处等量的减排来抵消一定量的碳排放或污染
senses.example: The firm offset its flights by funding a forest project.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司通过资助一个森林项目来抵消其航班的排放。
senses.why: Climate policy borrowed the accounting verb and made the two pans visible as emissions and removals.
senses.whyCN: 气候政策借用了这个会计动词，把天平两端的排放与移除摆到明面上。

intro.en: Offset is an English compound of off and set, first meaning to set out or start, later to place one thing against another. The printing sense arrived in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: 这是英语中由 off 与 set 构成的复合词，最初意为「出发、开始」，后来指「把一物对着另一物摆放」；印刷义在十九世纪出现。

items.en: Set goes back to Old English settan, to place or cause to sit, and it supplies the placing half of the compound.
items.cn: set 可追溯到古英语 settan「放置、使坐」，提供这个复合词「摆放」的那一半。

items.en: Off marks separation or away, so offset began as a placing away from the main line.
items.cn: off 标出分离或离开，所以这个词最初指「放在主线之外」。

items.en: The early verb meant to set out on a journey, a sense now carried by set off rather than offset.
items.cn: 早期动词义为「出发上路」，这一义今天由「出发」那一短语承担，而不是本词。

items.en: The accounting and balancing sense developed later; the exact date of that shift is uncertain and is usually given only as the early modern period.
items.cn: 会计与抵消义后来才发展出来；这一转变的确切年代不确定，通常只给近代早期这一约数。

items.en: Offset printing named the transfer of ink from plate to blanket to paper, an indirect set-off.
items.cn: 胶印得名于油墨从印版转到橡皮布再到纸上的间接转印。

items.en: Carbon offset extended the accounting image to emissions, with one pan holding what is released and the other what is removed.
items.cn: 碳抵消把会计画面扩展到排放，一端放释放的量，另一端放移除的量。

note.en: The first group looks close or shares the set root; the second group names neighbouring ideas of compensation.
note.cn: 第一组与「offset」形近或共享 set 词根；第二组是与「补偿」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The present participle and noun for the act of balancing one item against another.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词与名词，指把一项对着另一项抵消。

entries.definition: A phrasal verb meaning to start a journey or to trigger something.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，指出发或触发。

entries.definition: The beginning of something, from the same set with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指开端，由同一个表示「放置」的词根配不同前缀。

entries.definition: The machine used in offset printing.
entries.definitionCN: 胶印所用的机器。

entries.definition: A reversal or delay, from set and back rather than set and off.
entries.definitionCN: 指挫折或延误，由表示「放置」的词与表示「向后」的词构成。

entries.definition: To weigh against something with equal force.
entries.definitionCN: 指以相等的力量与之抗衡。

entries.definition: To make up for a loss or a disadvantage.
entries.definitionCN: 指弥补损失或劣势。

entries.definition: To bring two sides into equal weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指使两边重量相等。

entries.definition: To cancel the effect of something completely.
entries.definitionCN: 指彻底取消某物的作用。

entries.definition: To supply what is missing, in everyday wording.
entries.definitionCN: 指补上缺少的部分，日常说法。

entries.definition: To protect against a financial risk by an opposite position.
entries.definitionCN: 指用反向头寸防范金融风险。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two halves off and set, the accounting image and the printing trade term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用 off 与 set 两个部分、会计的天平画面，以及印刷行业术语。

normal.en: Off means away and set means place, so offset is to place one thing against another.
normal.cn: off 是「离开」，set 是「放置」，所以这个词就是把一物对着另一物放。

normal.en: The past tense does not change: offset, offset, offsetting.
normal.cn: 过去式不变：offset、offset、offsetting。

normal.en: Accounting says to offset an advance against an invoice.
normal.cn: 会计说把预付款与发票相抵。

normal.en: Printers speak of offset printing, where ink is transferred twice.
normal.cn: 印刷行话说胶印，油墨要转印两次。

normal.en: Carbon offset is the modern phrase for balancing emissions with removals.
normal.cn: 碳抵消是用移除量平衡排放量的现代说法。

abstract.en: To offset is to admit that a gain and a loss can sit on the same scale.
abstract.cn: 抵消，就是承认一份得与一份失可以放在同一架天平上。

abstract.en: Nothing is undone by offsetting; the scale simply returns to level.
abstract.cn: 抵消并没有撤销什么，只是让天平回到水平。

abstract.en: Every saving you find is a weight you may later place against a cost you cannot avoid.
abstract.cn: 你找到的每一笔节省，都是日后可以放到无法避免的开支对面的重量。

examples.en: Fuel savings offset the higher purchase price within three years.
examples.cn: 燃油节省在三年内抵消了更高的购价。

examples.en: The charity offsets its office emissions by planting trees.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构通过植树抵消办公排放。

examples.en: The pipe was offset slightly to clear the beam.
examples.cn: 为了避开梁，这根管子被略微偏移。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥夫塞特」——天平一端压账单，一端放硬币：抵消、补偿

root: 英语复合词，由表示「离开」的前缀与表示「放置」的古英语动词构成；先指出发，后指抵消与错开摆放；印刷义为十九世纪。抵消义的确切转变年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses put two things on opposite pans: cost, loss, shortfall, risk, position, accounts, print and emissions.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把两样东西放到天平两端：成本、损失、缺口、风险、位置、账目、印刷与排放。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bill sits on one pan and a stack of coins on the other until the beam levels.
core.cn: 核心意象：一端压着账单，另一端放上硬币，横梁慢慢回到水平。

branches.en: THE TWO COLUMNS: an extra cost meets a saving, and the books are made to agree.
branches.cn: 两栏相对：额外开支遇上节省，账目被做成相符。

branches.en: THE GAP IS FILLED: a loss or a shortfall is covered from the other side.
branches.cn: 缺口被填：损失或不足由另一端补上。

branches.en: THE RISK IS HEDGED: a position is deliberately placed opposite to a threat.
branches.cn: 风险被对冲：有意把一笔头寸摆在威胁的对面。

branches.en: THE LINE IS SHIFTED: an object leaves its original alignment.
branches.cn: 线条被挪开：物体离开原来的对齐位置。

branches.en: THE INDIRECT TRANSFER: ink or emissions are set off onto another surface or account.
branches.cn: 间接转印：油墨或排放被转到另一表面或另一本账上。

intro.en: Offset is a native English compound, so its parts are ordinary English words and its endings are English endings.
intro.cn: 这是一个英语本族复合词，其组成部分是普通英语词，词尾也是英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for this compound; the Latin column stays empty rather than importing unrelated forms.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词没有拉丁语来源，拉丁部分留空，不引入无关形式。

items.exampleCN: 它标出这个复合词中的位移。

items.example: It supplies the placing half of the word.

items.example: The Old English form behind modern set.

items.example: The same form serves as verb and noun.
items.exampleCN: 同一形式兼作动词与名词。

items.example: The trade name preserves the transfer image.

items.example: It extends the accounting image to climate.
items.exampleCN: 它把会计画面扩展到气候。

items.example: It shows set with a different prefix.

definition_zh: 后代；子女；（动物的）幼崽；（植物的）子代
definition_en: the young produced by a parent, whether human, animal or plant

scene: 巢边的母鸟把虫子塞进三张张开的嘴里，雏鸟的绒毛还没退。The offspring stayed in the nest for another three weeks before they could fly.
sceneCN: 这里 offspring 指「幼鸟；后代」（第 3 个义项：动物所产的幼体）；句意：这些幼鸟在巢里又待了三周才学会飞。图中可辨识物件：鸟巢、母鸟、三只雏鸟、碎蛋壳。

pos.zh: 后代；子女；幼崽（单复数同形）

senses.title: Biological descendants
senses.titleCN: 生物后代：延续下来的个体
senses.definition: the new individuals produced by a parent organism
senses.definitionCN: 亲本生物所产生的新的个体
senses.example: Each pair raised four offspring in the season.
senses.exampleCN: 每对鸟在这一季育出四只后代。
senses.why: off means 'away from' and spring means 'to arise', so the word pictures new life arising from a parent.
senses.whyCN: off 意为「离开」，spring 意为「涌出」，因此这个词描绘新生命从亲本涌出。

senses.title: A person's children
senses.definition: the children of a person, used in formal or neutral writing
senses.definitionCN: 某人的子女，用于正式或中性写作
senses.example: The estate passed to his offspring.
senses.exampleCN: 这份产业传给了他的子女。
senses.why: the same word serves humans, which is why it appears in legal and formal prose where 'children' feels too warm.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也用于人，因此在法律与正式文本中取代了显得过于亲昵的「孩子」。

senses.title: The young of an animal
senses.titleCN: 动物幼崽：一窝里的幼体
senses.definition: the young of an animal, especially before independence
senses.definitionCN: 动物所产的幼体，尤指尚未独立时
senses.example: The fox moved her offspring to a new den at night.
senses.exampleCN: 母狐夜里把幼崽搬到新的洞穴。
senses.why: in zoology the word is neutral about number, so a whole brood can be called offspring.
senses.whyCN: 在动物学中这个词对数量中立，因此一整窝都可叫 offspring。

senses.title: A product or result, literary
senses.definition: something that arises as a result of another thing, in elevated or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 由另一事物产生的结果，用于高雅或文学语境
senses.example: The theory was an offspring of wartime engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 这套理论是战时工程的产物。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the parent-child shape and applies it to ideas and institutions.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻保留了亲子形状，并把它用到观念与制度上。

senses.title: Plant progeny
senses.definition: the seeds, seedlings or daughter plants produced by a parent plant
senses.definitionCN: 母株所产生的种子、幼苗或子株
senses.example: The orchard's offspring were planted in a new row.
senses.exampleCN: 果园的子代被栽到新的一行。
senses.why: botany extends the animal word to plants, where the 'young' may be a seed rather than a mobile creature.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把这个动物词扩展到植物，这里的「幼体」可以是一粒种子而非会动的生物。

senses.title: Hybrid progeny
senses.titleCN: 杂交后代：两个亲本的子代
senses.definition: the young produced by a cross between two varieties or species
senses.definitionCN: 两个品种或物种杂交所产生的子代
senses.example: The hybrid offspring were sterile in the first generation.
senses.exampleCN: 杂交后代在第一代是不育的。
senses.why: breeding needs a word that covers the result of a cross without naming the species.
senses.whyCN: 育种需要一个词来指杂交结果，而不点明物种。

senses.title: The filial generation in genetics
senses.definition: a generation in a breeding experiment, labelled F1, F2 and so on
senses.definitionCN: 育种实验中的一代，标记为 F1、F2 等
senses.example: The F1 offspring all showed the dominant trait.
senses.exampleCN: F1 子代全部表现出显性性状。
senses.why: experimental genetics counts generations, and offspring becomes a countable unit in a cross.
senses.whyCN: 实验遗传学按代计数，offspring 便成为杂交中的可数单位。

senses.title: A figurative successor
senses.titleCN: 比喻的继承者：事业的后来者
senses.definition: a person or group that continues an earlier person's work or tradition
senses.definitionCN: 延续前人或传统之工作的人或群体
senses.example: The new institute saw itself as the offspring of the old school.
senses.exampleCN: 新研究所把自己看作老学派的继承者。
senses.why: the last branch loosens biology entirely: what is inherited is a tradition rather than genes.
senses.whyCN: 最后一支完全松开生物学：被继承的是传统而非基因。

intro.en: Offspring is a native English compound of off 'away' and spring 'to arise, to leap up'. It has no Latin root, and dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: offspring 是英语本族复合词，由 off「离开」与 spring「涌出、跃起」构成。它没有拉丁词根，以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Old English ofspring meant 'children, descendants, fruit of the body', built from of 'from' and springan 'to spring, arise'.
items.cn: 古英语 ofspring 意为「子女、后代、身体的果实」，由 of「从」与 springan「涌出、产生」构成。

items.en: The verb springan meant 'to leap, burst forth, arise', and also gave the season name spring, when growth bursts out.
items.cn: 动词 springan 意为「跳跃、迸出、产生」，也给出季节名 spring，即万物迸发的时节。

items.en: The form settled as offspring, with the sense of a person's children or an animal's young.
items.cn: 形式固定为 offspring，指人的子女或动物的幼体。

items.en: Nineteenth-century biology made offspring a general term for the young of any organism, including plants.
items.cn: 19 世纪生物学使 offspring 成为任何生物（含植物）幼体的通称。

items.en: Breeding experiments gave the word a countable place in generation labels such as F1 offspring.
items.cn: 育种实验让这个词在 F1 子代等世代标记中获得可数位置。

items.en: First dates are approximate; the plural has been unchanged since Old English, and the form offsprings is rare and nonstandard.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数；复数自古英语起就不加 -s，offsprings 罕见且不合规范。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes built from spring and off; group two holds near terms for the young of a parent.
note.cn: 第一组是由 spring 与 off 构成的形近词；第二组是近义术语，均指亲本所产的幼体。

entries.definition: A season, a coil, a water source or the act of leaping. Only in the compound does it mean descent.
entries.definitionCN: 指季节、弹簧、泉源或跳跃；只有在复合词中才表示血统。

entries.definition: A side branch of a plant or an organisation. It is derived from the same off-, but names a division rather than young.
entries.definitionCN: 指植物或组织的侧枝；同由 off- 构成，但指分支而非幼体。

entries.definition: A counterbalance, or a short shoot that roots beside the parent. It is not the general word for descendants.
entries.definitionCN: 指抵消，或母株旁生根的短枝；不是后代的通称。

entries.definition: The period when business or sport is quiet, built with off- meaning 'away from the main period'. It shares only the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指生意或赛事的淡季，off- 表「离开主要时段」；只共享前缀。

entries.definition: Away from the stage area, with off- meaning 'away'. The shared prefix is the only link.
entries.definitionCN: 指离开舞台区域，off- 表「离开」；只共享前缀而已。

entries.definition: Descendants treated as a group, from Latin progignere 'to bring forth'. It is more formal than offspring.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为群体的后代，出自拉丁 progignere「产生」；比 offspring 更正式。

entries.definition: The offspring of an animal while still young, or the state of being young. It is not used for human children in the same way.
entries.definitionCN: 指动物尚幼时的后代，或年轻的状态；不用于人的子女。

entries.definition: The plural of child, used for people and carrying an emotional tone that offspring lacks.
entries.definitionCN: child 的复数，用于人，带有 offspring 所缺的情感色彩。

entries.definition: A person or organism in a line of descent, possibly many generations later. Offspring usually means the immediate young.
entries.definitionCN: 指血统线上的一个人或生物，可能隔许多代；offspring 通常指直接的幼体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: off 'from' + spring 'to arise': new life arising from a parent.
normal.cn: off「从」+ spring「涌出」：从亲本涌出的新生命。

normal.en: The family runs spring, offshoot, offset, offspring; progeny is a formal synonym.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 spring、offshoot、offset、offspring；progeny 是正式同义词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: produce offspring, viable offspring, number of offspring, offspring survival.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：产生后代、可存活的后代、后代数量、后代存活。

normal.en: The plural never takes -s in standard use; offspring is already plural.
normal.cn: 标准用法中复数不加 -s；offspring 本身即复数。

normal.en: Genetics counts it by generation: F1 offspring, then F2.
normal.cn: 遗传学按代计数：先是 F1 子代，再是 F2。

abstract.en: Picture three open beaks in a nest, all pointed at one parent.
abstract.cn: 想象巢里三张张开的嘴，全都朝向同一只亲鸟。

abstract.en: Picture a seed dropping from a parent tree onto bare soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子从母树落到裸土上。

abstract.en: Picture a school of thought branching off an older one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个学派从更老的学派中分支出来。

examples.en: The pair produced six offspring over three breeding seasons.
examples.cn: 这对鸟在三个繁殖季里育出六只后代。

examples.en: Hybrid offspring often show traits intermediate between the parents.
examples.cn: 杂交后代常表现出介于两亲本之间的性状。

examples.en: The foundation regarded the new lab as its intellectual offspring.
examples.cn: 基金会把这个新实验室视为自己的学术后代。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离开（off）母体、涌出（spring）的新生命」——从亲本身上冒出来的一代 → 后代

root: 古英语 of「从」+ springan「涌出、跃起」→ ofspring「子女、后代」；英语本族复合词，无拉丁词根；复数形式自古英语起不变。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: new life arises from a parent, as animals' young, people's children, plants' seed, hybrid crosses, experimental generations, or a tradition's successor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个意象展开：新生命从亲本涌出——动物的幼体、人的子女、植物的种子、杂交子代、实验世代，或传统的继承者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: open beaks in a nest, all pointing at the parent bird.
core.cn: 核心意象：巢里张开的喙，全都朝向亲鸟。

branches.en: ANIMAL YOUNG: the literal descendants, counted as a brood.
branches.cn: 动物幼体：字面的后代，按窝计数。

branches.en: HUMAN CHILDREN: the same word in formal and legal prose.
branches.cn: 人的子女：同一个词用于正式与法律文本。

branches.en: METAPHOR: ideas, institutions and traditions arise from earlier ones.
branches.cn: 隐喻：观念、制度与传统由更早者产生。

branches.en: PLANTS: seed and seedling carry the line.
branches.cn: 植物：种子与幼苗延续血脉。

branches.en: BREEDING: crosses and labelled generations make the word countable.
branches.cn: 育种：杂交与世代标记使这个词可数。

intro.en: The word is a native English compound of a preposition and a verb stem; it takes no Latin prefix or suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族复合词，由介词与动词词干构成；不含拉丁前缀或后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin family. The nearest formal synonyms are borrowed: progeny from progignere and descendant from descendere.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁词族。最近的正式同义词是借来的：progeny 出自 progignere，descendant 出自 descendere。

definition_zh: 省略；遗漏；不提及；排除在外
definition_en: to leave something out on purpose, to fail to include it by mistake, to say nothing about it, or to keep someone or something off a list
core_image: 一张写好的名单上，中间一行被人用笔轻轻划掉，留下一道细线
scene: 办公室的灯还亮着，编辑把打印稿铺在桌上，逐行核对后又用笔尖划去其中一行名字。One name was omitted from the final list.
sceneCN: 这里的 omitted 是「被删去、未被列入」（第 1 个义项：有意删去）；句意为最终名单上有一个名字被删掉了。图中可辨识物件：打印稿、笔尖、名单。

pos.zh: 省略；遗漏；不提及；排除在外

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 omittere 的词干 omiss- 加 -ion 构成，义为「省略；遗漏」
由 omiss- 加 -ible 构成，义为「可以省略的」
由 omiss- 加 -ive 构成，义为「省略的；遗漏的」

senses.title: Leaving something out on purpose
senses.definition: to leave out a word, detail or step deliberately, so that it is not included
senses.definitionCN: 有意不把某个词、细节或步骤放进去，使其不被包含在内
senses.example: The editor omitted the last paragraph to save space.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑删去了最后一段以节省篇幅。
senses.why: Latin omittere meant to let go or let pass, so leaving something out is pictured as releasing it rather than destroying it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 omittere 意为放走、让过去，所以「省去」被想成把东西放开，而不是把它毁掉。

senses.title: Leaving something out by mistake
senses.definition: to fail to include or do something because one forgot or overlooked it
senses.definitionCN: 因为忘记或看漏而没有把某事列入或没有去做
senses.example: Two names were omitted from the guest list by accident.
senses.exampleCN: 有两个名字被无意中漏在了宾客名单之外。
senses.why: The same act of letting something pass can happen with or without intent, and English keeps one verb for both the planned and the accidental gap.
senses.whyCN: 同样一个「让它过去」的动作，可能有意也可能无意，英语用同一个动词兼指计划中的空缺和疏忽造成的空缺。

senses.title: Saying nothing about something
senses.definition: to say nothing about something, whether from carelessness or from a wish to avoid it
senses.definitionCN: 对某事一字不提，不论是出于疏忽还是有意回避
senses.example: He omitted any mention of the delay in his report.
senses.exampleCN: 他在报告里对延误只字未提。
senses.why: If a word can be left out of a text, it can also be left out of speech, so the verb comes to mean passing over a matter in silence.
senses.whyCN: 一个词能从文本里省掉，也能从话语里省掉，于是这个动词就表示对一件事沉默地略过。

senses.title: Keeping someone off a list or group
senses.definition: to leave a person or thing out of a set, list or team, often as a decision
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物排除在一套名单或队伍之外，常是经过决定的
senses.example: The coach omitted him from the squad for the final.
senses.exampleCN: 教练把他排除在决赛的队员名单之外。
senses.why: A list is a set of chosen items, and whatever is not chosen is let go, so omission becomes a quiet way of excluding.
senses.whyCN: 名单是一组被选中项，凡没被选中的就被放开，于是「省去」也成了一种安静的排除方式。

intro.en: Omit comes from Latin omittere, a verb built from a prefix meaning away and mittere, to send or let go; the idea of releasing something explains why the word covers both deliberate cuts and accidental gaps.
intro.cn: omit 来自拉丁语 omittere，由表示「离开」的前缀与 mittere（送出、放走）构成；「把东西放开」这个想法解释了它为何兼指有意删削与无意遗漏。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go, and it supplied the moving force inside a large family of English verbs.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放走，为英语一大族动词提供了内在的「送出」力量。

items.en: Ob- plus mittere, worn down to om-, gave omittere, to let go or let pass by, and its participle stem was omiss-.
items.cn: ob- 与 mittere 合成并磨变为 om-，得到 omittere，意为放走、让过去，其分词词干为 omiss-。

items.en: Old French took the verb as ometre, meaning to leave out or to fail to do, and used it of words and duties alike.
items.cn: 古法语借作 ometre，意为略去、漏做，词与职责都能接。

items.en: Middle English adopted it as omitten, and the modern spelling omit replaced the older ending in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语作 omitten，到十六世纪现代拼写 omit 取代了旧词尾。

items.en: Modern English keeps omit for leaving out words, facts, steps and people, and doubles the t in omitted and omitting because the stress falls on the last syllable.
items.cn: 现代英语让 omit 承担略去词语、事实、步骤与人，并因重音落在末音节而在 omitted、omitting 中双写 t。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin verb mittere, which is about sending; the near-meaning group collects verbs for leaving things or people out.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁动词 mittere（送出）上的词；近义组收表示把事物或人排除在外的动词。

entries.definition: The act or result of leaving something out.

entries.definitionCN: 把某物从计划、名单或文本中去掉。

normalIntro.en: Omit hides a Latin verb of sending under a prefix meaning away, so every hook pictures something being let go rather than deleted.
normalIntro.cn: omit 在表示「离开」的前缀下藏着一个拉丁语「送出」动词，所以每条记忆钩子都想着某物被放开，而不是被删除。

normal.en: The visible part of omit is the Latin verb mittere, to send, and the prefix om- marks the movement away.
normal.cn: omit 看得见的部分是拉丁动词 mittere（送出），前缀 om- 标出「离开」的方向。

normal.en: Omitted and omitting double the t because the stress sits on the final syllable, as in admitted and permitting.
normal.cn: omitted 与 omitting 双写 t，因为重音落在最后一个音节，就像 admitted 与 permitting 一样。

normal.en: Omission is built on the participle stem omiss- plus -ion, the noun suffix for an act or its result.
normal.cn: omission 建立在分词词干 omiss- 上，加 -ion 这个表示行为或结果的名词后缀。

normal.en: Emit, submit and permit share the same mittere, so the family is about sending, not about leaving out.
normal.cn: emit、submit、permit 共用同一个 mittere，可见这一族词讲的是送出，而不是省去。

normal.en: Omit to mention is a fixed pattern meaning to forget to say, and it keeps the old sense of letting a duty pass.
normal.cn: omit to mention 是固定说法，意为忘记说，它保留了「让一项职责溜过去」的旧意思。

abstract.en: A gap can be a decision or an accident, and English lets one word hold both without apology.
abstract.cn: 一个空缺可以出于决定，也可以出于意外，而英语让同一个词把两者都装下，不作区分。

abstract.en: To omit is to trust that the missing piece will be noticed only when it matters.
abstract.cn: 省去，就是相信缺失的那一块只有在要紧时才会被人察觉。

abstract.en: The same verb that removes a word also removes a person, which shows how thin the line is between editing and exclusion.
abstract.cn: 删掉一个词的动词也能排除一个人，这说明编辑与排斥之间的界线多么细。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把某物放开；义项按意图与对象分出有意删削、无意遗漏、沉默不提与排除在外。

definition_zh: 杂食性的；什么都吃的；兴趣广泛的
definition_en: describing an animal or person that consumes both plant and animal material, or more broadly one with very wide tastes
core_image: 一张餐桌上同时摆着谷物、浆果、鱼与昆虫，一把叉子伸向每一种
scene: 这里指「杂食性的」。 The omnivorous bear eats berries in July and salmon in September.

senses.title: Eating both diets
senses.titleCN: 杂食性：植物与动物性食物兼食
senses.definition: describing an animal that eats both plant and animal material in substantial amounts
senses.definitionCN: 描述大量食用植物与动物性材料两者的动物
senses.example: The omnivorous diet of the fox includes fruit, insects and small mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 狐狸的杂食食谱包括果实、昆虫与小型哺乳动物。
senses.why: The adjective marks the mixed-diet class, which is neither herbivorous nor carnivorous.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出混合食性类别，既非植食也非食肉。

senses.title: Bears and other switch eaters
senses.definition: describing animals such as bears that shift between plant and animal foods as seasons change
senses.definitionCN: 描述熊这类随季节在植物性与动物性食物之间切换的动物
senses.example: Omnivorous bears gain weight on berries before the salmon run.
senses.exampleCN: 杂食的熊在鲑鱼洄游前靠浆果增重。
senses.why: Seasonal switching is the practical advantage of the class: the animal is never stuck with one failing food.
senses.whyCN: 季节切换是这一类的实际优势：动物不会困在单一失败的食物上。

senses.title: Omnivorous birds
senses.titleCN: 杂食鸟类：谷物、昆虫与腐肉都吃
senses.definition: describing birds that take seeds, fruit, insects, eggs or carrion depending on opportunity
senses.definitionCN: 描述视机会取食种子、果实、昆虫、卵或腐肉的鸟类
senses.example: Omnivorous birds adapt quickly when a crop fails.
senses.exampleCN: 作物歉收时，杂食鸟类能迅速适应。
senses.why: Flight lets birds sample many patches, which makes a mixed diet especially efficient.
senses.whyCN: 飞行让鸟类能采样许多斑块，因此混合食性尤其高效。

senses.title: Omnivorous insects
senses.titleCN: 杂食昆虫：既取食植物也取食动物
senses.definition: describing insects that feed on plant tissue and on other animals or carrion
senses.definitionCN: 描述既取食植物组织、也取食其他动物或腐肉的昆虫
senses.example: Omnivorous ants scavenge seeds, insects and dead vertebrates.
senses.exampleCN: 杂食蚂蚁取食种子、昆虫与死亡脊椎动物。
senses.why: Many ants are the clearest examples, because a colony can exploit several food channels at once.
senses.whyCN: 许多蚂蚁是最清楚的例子，因为一个蚁群能同时利用多条食物通道。

senses.title: The human mixed diet
senses.titleCN: 人类混合饮食：谷物与肉并用
senses.definition: describing the human species' capacity to live on a combination of plant and animal foods
senses.definitionCN: 描述人类物种靠植物与动物性食物组合生活的能力
senses.example: Human beings are omnivorous and can survive on many different food mixes.
senses.exampleCN: 人类是杂食性的，能靠许多不同的食物组合生存。
senses.why: The adjective is used at species level in nutrition, describing a capacity rather than a recommended diet.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在营养学中用于物种层面，描述一种能力，而不是推荐食谱。

senses.title: An omnivorous reader
senses.titleCN: 什么书都读的人：阅读范围极广
senses.definition: figuratively describing a person who reads widely across genres, subjects and levels of difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 比喻描述跨越体裁、主题与难度广泛阅读的人
senses.example: She is an omnivorous reader who moves from biology to detective novels.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个什么书都读的人，从生物学读到侦探小说。
senses.why: The dietary metaphor turns reading into eating: the reader consumes every kind of text.
senses.whyCN: 饮食比喻把阅读变成进食：读者消耗各种文本。

senses.title: Omnivorous curiosity
senses.titleCN: 无所不包的求知欲：什么都想了解
senses.definition: figuratively describing an appetite for knowledge that ranges across unrelated fields
senses.definitionCN: 比喻描述横跨不相关领域的求知欲望
senses.example: His omnivorous curiosity led him from fossils to finance.
senses.exampleCN: 他无所不包的求知欲把他从化石带到金融。
senses.why: The metaphor extends from texts to questions, where the 'food' is any subject at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻从文本扩展到问题，这里的「食物」可以是任何主题。

senses.title: Cultural and media omnivorousness
senses.titleCN: 文化杂食：品味与平台都不设限
senses.definition: in sociology and media studies, describing a taste or usage pattern that crosses highbrow, popular and multiple platforms
senses.definitionCN: 社会学与媒介研究中描述跨越高雅、通俗与多种平台的品味或使用模式
senses.example: The study found an omnivorous pattern of news consumption across print, video and social media.
senses.exampleCN: 研究发现了一种跨纸媒、视频与社交媒体的杂食型新闻消费模式。
senses.why: The adjective has become a technical term for boundary-crossing, not merely for eating everything.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词已成为描述跨界的技术术语，不再只是「什么都吃」。

intro.en: Omnivorous is a scientific Latin adjective from omnis 'all' and vorare 'devour', older than the English noun omnivore.
intro.cn: omnivorous 是科学拉丁语形容词，由 omnis「全部」与 vorare「吞食」构成，比英语名词 omnivore 更早。

items.en: Omnis meant all or every, and its prefix form omni- spread into words about power, knowledge and transport.
items.cn: omnis 意为全部、每个，其前缀形式 omni- 扩散到关于权力、知识与交通的词中。

items.en: Vorare meant to devour, the eating verb shared with herbivorous and carnivorous.
items.cn: vorare 意为吞食，与 herbivorous、carnivorous 共用的吃的动词。

items.en: Omnivorus was the adjective for a mixed diet in modern scientific Latin. Its exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: omnivorus 是近代科学拉丁语中表示混合食性的形容词；确切首用存疑。

items.en: English omnivorous is recorded in the seventeenth century and was soon used figuratively for broad reading. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 omnivorous 见于 17 世纪，很快被比喻用于广泛阅读；确切首见书证存疑。

items.en: Sociology and media studies turned omnivorous into a term for crossing cultural and platform boundaries in the late twentieth century.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期，社会学与媒介研究把 omnivorous 变成描述跨越文化与平台边界的术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vorous ending; the near-meaning group separates mixed diet from wide interest and technical breadth.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -vorous 结尾；近义组区分混合食性、广泛兴趣与技术性广度。

entries.definition: The animal or person itself. It is a count noun, so a bear is an omnivore with an omnivorous diet.
entries.definitionCN: 指动物或人本身。它是可数名词，因此熊是 omnivore，其食谱是 omnivorous。

entries.definition: Describes a plant-only diet. The stem herba- replaces omni- and reverses the class.
entries.definitionCN: 描述纯植食。词干 herba- 替换 omni-，类别随之相反。

entries.definition: Describes a flesh-only diet. The stem caro- replaces omni-, and the diet narrows.
entries.definitionCN: 描述纯肉食。词干 caro- 替换 omni-，食性随之收窄。

entries.definition: A species or person that uses many resources. It is broader than omnivorous, which is specifically about food.
entries.definitionCN: 指利用多种资源的物种或人。它比 omnivorous 更宽，后者专指食物。

entries.definition: Describes tastes drawn from many sources. It matches the figurative sense of omnivorous but is used of style and choice, not diet.
entries.definitionCN: 描述从多种来源汲取的品味。它对应 omnivorous 的比喻义，但用于风格与选择，而非食性。

entries.definition: A technical adjective for feeding on many kinds of food, mostly used of insects. It overlaps with omnivorous but belongs to entomology.
entries.definitionCN: 技术形容词，指取食多种食物，多用于昆虫。它与 omnivorous 重叠，但属昆虫学用语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: omni 'all' + -vorous 'eating': eating everything.
normal.cn: omni「全部」+ -vorous「吃……的」：什么都吃。

normal.en: Typical phrases: omnivorous animal, omnivorous diet, omnivorous reader, omnivorous curiosity.
normal.cn: 典型搭配：杂食动物、杂食食谱、什么书都读的人、无所不包的求知欲。

normal.en: The family runs omnivore, omnivory, omnibus and omni- words such as omnipotent.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 omnivore、omnivory、omnibus，以及 omnipotent 这类 omni- 词。

normal.en: Swap the stem to change the class: omni-, herbi-, carni-.
normal.cn: 换词干就换类别：omni-、herbi-、carni-。

normal.en: In sociology, omnivorous means boundary-crossing taste, not literal eating.
normal.cn: 在社会学中，omnivorous 指跨界的品味，而非字面进食。

abstract.en: Picture one table holding grain, berries, fish and insects, with a fork reaching everywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌上摆着谷物、浆果、鱼与昆虫，叉子伸向每一处。

abstract.en: Picture a reader with a biology paper and a detective novel open at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一位读者同时摊开一篇生物学论文和一本侦探小说。

abstract.en: Picture one person reading news in print, on video and on a phone before noon.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在中午前就从纸媒、视频与手机上读新闻。

examples.en: The omnivorous bear moves from berries to salmon as autumn arrives.
examples.cn: 秋天到来时，这只杂食的熊从浆果转向鲑鱼。

examples.en: Omnivorous ants exploit both seeds and dead insects.
examples.cn: 杂食蚂蚁既利用种子也利用死昆虫。

examples.en: Her omnivorous reading made her hard to surprise in conversation.
examples.cn: 她什么书都读，交谈时很难被难住。

dict_mnemonic.text: omnivore（杂食动物）+ ous（……的）→ 杂食的 → omnivorous

root: 拉丁 omnis「全部」+ vorare「吞食」→ 科学拉丁语 omnivorus「各类食物都吃的」→ 英语 omnivorous。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one adjective to diet, seasonal switching, birds, insects, human capacity, reading, curiosity and cultural breadth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个形容词用于食性、季节切换、鸟类、昆虫、人类能力、阅读、求知欲与文化广度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one table holding grain, berries, fish and insects, reached from every side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌上摆着谷物、浆果、鱼与昆虫，四面都能取用。

branches.en: DIET: mixed eating is the base, and seasonal switching is its practical payoff.
branches.cn: 食性：混合取食是基本义，季节切换是它的实际收益。

branches.en: ANIMALS: birds and insects show the class across very different body plans.
branches.cn: 动物：鸟类与昆虫展示了这一类在差异极大的体型中的表现。

branches.en: HUMANS: the adjective describes a species-level capacity, not a menu plan.
branches.cn: 人类：这个形容词描述物种层面的能力，而非一份菜单。

branches.en: METAPHOR: reading and curiosity become forms of eating.
branches.cn: 比喻：阅读与求知欲变成进食的形式。

branches.en: TECHNICAL: sociology uses the word for taste that crosses every boundary.
branches.cn: 技术用法：社会学用这个词描述跨越一切边界的品味。

intro.en: Omnivorous is the adjective branch of the 'all-eating' family, and omni- is one of the most transparent prefixes in English.
intro.cn: omnivorous 是「什么都吃」词族的形容词支，omni- 是英语中最透明的前缀之一。

latinIntro.en: Omnis means all, vorare means devour, and -vorus is the scientific adjective ending used across diet words.
latinIntro.cn: omnis 意为全部，vorare 意为吞食，-vorus 是各类食性词共用的科学形容词词尾。

items.meaningCN: 什么都吃的；兴趣广泛的
items.example: The omnivorous fish takes plants and larvae.
items.exampleCN: 这种杂食鱼既吃植物也吃幼虫。

items.example: The omnivore samples every food patch.
items.exampleCN: 这只杂食动物尝试每一处食物斑块。
杂食性在蚂蚁中很常见。

items.example: Omni- also forms omnipotent and omniscient.
items.exampleCN: omni- 还构成 omnipotent 与 omniscient。

items.example: The omnibus edition collects all four novels.
items.exampleCN: 合集版收录了全部四部小说。

items.example: Omnivorous species are often habitat generalists.
items.exampleCN: 杂食物种常常也是生境广适种。

items.example: The exhibit is eclectic in style.
